### 59.67 Sweep repairs: the mixing word boundary and empty bands

The first sweep reached 4,952 of its 7,256 selected cases: 4,688 passed,
31 failed, 232 skipped and one xpassed, in 1,051.120 seconds. I interrupted
it to repair the non-learning failures. Both stopping gates passed in
that run. This is an incomplete diagnostic sweep, not the required final
sweep; the remaining 2,304 cases did not complete.

**Mixing still staged objects.** Removing the arrival-time exchange left
`_stage_reading_grammar_references` publishing only object codes. There
was no own-word code for the new leaf law on this path, while its inverse
bank and `_pushed_word_slab` still described objects. The unchanged,
untrained forced-prefix fixture reconstructed only `hello` or `loving`
from each two-word input: 0/4 correct multisets on both reads, with first
read residuals 52,52,52,52 and second read residuals
13.75,15.25,15.75,14.25. HEAD on the fixture's original saved stream gives
4/4 on each read and all residuals zero. A process-local diagnostic
staging word codes restores those results without training or changing
a chooser; the production repair follows that boundary, not the test's
expected strings.

`Models._stage_reading_grammar_references` now stages each admitted word's
row, order, code and lexical form, separately from its current object
reference. `_stage_mixing_reconstruction_bank` reads those words;
`_pushed_word_slab`, `_capture_reading_programs`,
`_publish_sentence_scratch`, `_trial_understanding` and the final symbol
reference publication read word rows/codes/orders. They no longer
substitute `_ar_grammar_object_*` for the word tree. Those object arrays
remain for the existing mixing object staging and the protected
`ModelAttention.stage_expectation` reader; neither that reader nor its
forecast changes. `PrependedSymbols.refresh_words` updates the object's
references but does not replace a mixing inverse-bank word with that
object. Comprehension still selects the object after the walk.

The strengthened three-configuration word-deposit test exposed a second
producer: `stage_cs_lang` used `symbolic_orders`, the conceptual pass's
fold depth, as the word's order. All three cases failed (order 1 instead
of the staged word's order 0). Where an own-word code is staged, the push
now takes its row and order from the same staged word arrays. It keeps
the conceptual-pass metadata for paths without a word. This implements
the stated row/order part of the leaf law; it does not change allocation.
The three cases then pass. The earlier certificate's comparison of the
slot to the push alone did not catch this mismatch.

This supersedes §59.64's account of the mixing fallback. Admitted mixing
words now have their own code. Numeric inputs and paths without an
admitted word still retain their unsigned native event; no code or
reference is invented for them. The former object-bank override is

### 59.70 For Alec and Claude: bind compares the occurrence bands too

The unsigned sinusoids are built, but they expose an unported numerical
reader. `ReferenceContext.prepare_operands` calls `STMChunks.bind_menu`;
the latter calls `IdentityRows.meet_ratios` on every coordinate from
`meaning_start` onward. For a configuration with no separate meaning
block, `meaning_start` is zero. The word's location and time therefore
participate in the containment test alongside its content. They are
coordinates of where and when it was read, not more evidence of the
object's description.

In the unchanged live-reference fixture, the held idea contains every
content coordinate of the incoming word. The word and held idea have
different occurrence bands. The requested bind is unavailable at the
first word and after the second; the forced fixture consequently takes
`change` first and binds that result at the close. The later assertion
that the first participant already held the reference fails. Correcting
the separate word-order defect in §59.67 leaves this failure unchanged.

A minimal reproduction uses content (.2,.2) inside (.8,.8), locations 20
and 10, and ticks 1 and 0, with the actual codecs and native bind menu.
With the eight occurrence coordinates in the comparison, its two
containment ratios are approximately .8337 and .9677: the real candidate
is unavailable. Comparing the content alone gives .25 and 1: it is
available. In a process-local diagnostic on the unchanged live-reference
test, excluding only those eight coordinates from the **comparison**,
while returning the original candidates unchanged, offers the requested
bind before `change` and passes the original fusion assertion. The test
then reaches its separate old word-equals-pending-object assertion, which
requires the same §55.1.6 port as the inverse tests above. No such bind
comparison change is in production.

**Question:** may bind's containment read exclude the location/time band,
while keeping that band unchanged on the operand and selected result?
I recommend that rule: use content for containment, and retain location
and time for their own readers. This would also apply to the no-separate-
meaning configuration; the paired configuration already starts beyond
that band. It requires an explicit amendment because §68.62 rule 4 says
nothing downstream changes, naming `IdentityRows.meet_ratios` and its
readers, while §55.1.2 keeps the operators/chooser unchanged. Recentring
these coordinates only to recover the old test result would preserve the
same unwanted dependence, so I have not done that either.

Checkpoint source snapshot (`bounded_tests.source_snapshot`, 1,218 files):
`c1f6ac3004a5104987f8ca3cfaf9bd11ba43e0b552759698c5f98df1c6fce28d`.
No commit or push. The four protected attention files are byte-identical
to HEAD. There is no new edit in `Models._run_sentence_word_bricks` in
this continuation; its cumulative edits remain those in §59.51. In
`stage_cs_lang`, the continuation adds the unsigned own-word activation
and copies the product's occurrence band, uses the staged word row and
order rather than the conceptual pass's fold depth, and removes the
mixing-object fallback for the lexical scope ID. The earlier removal of
the object exchange and reference/publication witnesses are unchanged.
The final lesson/proof/assessment/sweep campaign remains owed after this
decision and the remaining ports; this is not a completion claim.

### 59.71 Resumed: containment reads content, occurrences keep their bands

Alec's continuation ("Please continue if that was the only stopper") is
taken as approval of §59.70's recommendation. `STMChunks.bind_menu` now
excludes the occurrence's location and time coordinates from its
containment comparison. It returns the original candidate, including
those coordinates, unchanged. `IdentityRows.meet_ratios` itself is
unchanged. The mask is applied by multiplication over the fixed-width
operands; the read introduces no variable-length gather.

The layout comes from the native LTM store in
`LanguageSpace.choose_operation`, through the new `percept_band`
argument of `ReferenceContext.prepare_operands`. In particular, the
journal's band cannot supply this information: an unpaired configuration
can have no journal band while its input still has the eight occurrence
coordinates. `prepare_operands` starts beyond the percept block only
when its interpreter's codebook actually has a separate meaning block;
otherwise it reads content across the unpaired code, excluding the band.
The live-reference fixture also supplies a reference bank without an
interpreter, so its old `meaning_start` was zero independently of the
native model's layout. This qualifies §59.70's explanation: the zero
start alone did not prove that this fixture's model was unpaired.

`test_public_reading_fuses_the_reference_before_capture_and_write`
failed its first-participant fusion assertion: the earlier bind was
unavailable. It now passes that assertion. The new parametrized
`test_bind_compares_content_and_preserves_occurrence_coordinates`
checks both layouts, offers the containing candidate despite different
location/time bands, rejects a genuinely incompatible description, and
checks exact preservation of the candidate and source state.

### 59.76 Final sweep diagnostics: inverse transport and two test ports

The diagnostic sweep reached 7,257 of 7,259 selected tests, including
both stopping gates, before being interrupted to finish the five failures
below and rerun on the completed source. It is not the final sweep.

1. `test_reading_curriculum.py::test_native_four_word_inverse_follows_composed_children_without_free_decoder[admitted-objects]`
   failed on 418 of 2,880 coordinates, maximum difference .2384058237.
   The saved failure stream fails with either bind containment. A selected
   `part` reads an object's value in place of a direct word leaf. The
   existing inverse discrepancy transport in
   `DerivationReconstruction.reconstruct` handled an intermediate child,
   but explicitly excluded a leaf. Thus the first word (with an intervening
   bind node) was transported, and the later direct leaves were not.
   The audit now transports a leaf when its recorded
   `operation_resolved` witness says that its operand was replaced. The
   producer is `program.leaves`, never the scored target. `inverse_step`
   and the training path are unchanged. The new
   `test_reconstruction_magnitudes.py::test_selected_reference_at_a_word_leaf_transports_inverse_error_not_the_target`
   fails before the repair and passes after: it retains a nonzero root
   error, its unit gradient, and independence from the scored target.
   The original assertion is unchanged. The saved native failure stream
   now passes both containment variants: **2 passed in 3.60 s**.
2. All three cases of
   `test_selected_nested_meaning.py::test_nested_observation_writers_retain_children_without_certifying_them`
   now receive the real leaf orders from `commit_reading`: (1,0,1).
   The existing class-close rule therefore keeps two occurrences of the
   order-one class, both at zero trust. The old assertion of no occurrence
   is ported to two zero-trust occurrences with that exact class referent;
   the relations address those occurrences. Every independent-pair,
   zero-evidence, parent-to-child, no-open-slot and detached-read assertion
   stays. The eight conceptual coordinates of this fixture have no time
   band; its helper uses STM0, of the same width and capacity, under
   §17.15 and the already accepted fixture rule of §23. It no longer
   presents those coordinates as an LTM0 time band. No writer changes.
3. `test_tetralemma_leaf.py::test_path_ast_has_no_pole_collapse` reported
   unlisted reads, not a cross-lane collapse. Its explicit census now
   includes `ClauseJournal._finish_clause` (the moved journal body) and
   `Comprehension.Evaluation.leaf` (the conversion's recorded evidence).
   The former takes each lane's minimum over words independently; the
   latter passes the pair to interpretation. The AST checker and its
   mutation assertions are unchanged.

The repaired/ported files, original inverse and live-reference tests,
unsigned certificates, item-55 mechanisms and both stopping gates give
**225 passed, 1 skipped in 37.39 s**. No expected-failure mark is added.

### 59.77 Correction of the unintended form-only bind change

On reading §68.65, I confirmed that §59.71 had also changed the start
of the comparison for a bank with an interpreter but no meaning pairs.
That was not part of §59.70's question. It allowed binding by forms,
contrary to the existing meaning-only contract. I have removed that
extra change: `ReferenceContext.prepare_operands` again takes
`mereology.percept_event_width` whenever that mereology exists, else
zero. Exclusion of the declared place/time band stays; the values and
references returned stay unchanged. This is a correction of my added
condition, not a new decision about what the menu should read.

`test_unsigned_coordinates.py::test_bind_bank_with_form_only_interpreter_offers_only_dummy`
uses identical forms. It fails with the extra condition (two valid
alternatives) and passes without it (only the dummy). The existing
both-layout and live-reference certificates pass too. No test requires
the changed start.

The cause in §59.70 is corrected: the signed bands already exposed the
comparison once the slot retained the word's identity. `STMChunks.refresh`
looks for an off-stack entry of the same identity and timeline; a word
with no such entry keeps its own value and occurrence bands. It still
refreshes a word if such a matching off-stack entry actually exists.
The unsigned encoding was not the producer of that change.

The lesson has a meaning block: its measured form width is **360** and
meaning width **32**. Its comparison starts at 360 before and after this
correction, so §59.74's lesson is unaffected by the restored start.
The inverse audit repair above has no production caller; its shared
`inverse_step` used by training is unchanged. The three file groups and
full sweep are nevertheless being run again on the completed source.

The final source at the start of those runs is
`e3936d459c868e0e472ada88023ed3d0609b4d0dd63c5dd45c41a799ace1bbb7`
(1,218 source files). §68.65's separate question about reading the word
versus its staged object in the menu is not implemented. The read,
chooser, order filter and exclusions are unchanged by this correction.

### 59.78 Additional read-only findings from the bind review

The passive four-file census uses `test_stm_chunk_gates.py`,
`test_item25_completion.py`, `test_math_chain.py` and
`test_live_references.py`. Both HEAD and the returned source pass all
**77 tests** (73.45 s and 77.42 s respectively). These are separate
unseeded runs, not a same-stream claim of numerical equivalence. Counts
include direct menu tests and forced grammar tests as well as native
reads. A candidate is a populated off-stack seat before containment;
mention orders are counted once per such candidate. A dummy is excluded
from “offered” and included in “binds chosen”.

| Read | HEAD | Returned source |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Menu calls | 286 | 425 |
| Candidates compared | 1,517 | 2,293 |
| Content passes | 131 | 259 |
| Content passes refused by order | 47 | 201 |
| Real candidates offered | 84 | 58 |
| Binds chosen, including dummy | 1 | 179 |
| Real binds chosen | 1 | 1 |
| Candidates at open mention order (-1) | 418 | 553 |
| Candidates at mention order 0 | 795 | 1,716 |
| Candidates at mention order 1 | 289 | 9 |
| Candidates at mention order 2 | 2 | 2 |
| Direct calls with no order argument | 13 | 13 |

This supports the review's distinction between containment and order;
it does not establish a correction for what the menu should read.
Nothing changes the mention, order filter or chooser for these counts.
The first diagnostic observer itself raised on a mock rule with no
`method_name`; that local observer was corrected to permit the mock.
There was no corresponding production failure.

The additional explicit numerical consumers of occurrence coordinates
noticed during this review are not phase decoders:

- `ReferenceClose.continuity` takes the sum of componentwise minima of
  stored `.where` bands as one policy feature. It still does so. The
  unsigned representation changes that feature; it is not a centered
  phase overlap. No claim of invariant continuity logits is made.
- `SubSpace._compute_active` and `set_activation_from_event` use nonzero
  band norms to mark presence. Present unsigned bands remain nonzero,
  and the absent all-zero sentinel remains zero.
- `ReferenceContext.resolve_operand` ranks its bounded candidates by a
  full-value squared residual and query norm. It has no independent band
  mask. This existing numerical reference reader is unchanged.

For the `IdentityRows.meet_ratios` call census, the following reads can
reach occurrence coordinates without `IdentityRows.coordinates` first:
`ClauseRows.consequents` and `evaluate` when `ChainRead.point` reads an
occurrence; `MediumTermMemory.merge` for a state/event/percept collection;
and the percept branch of `MemoryLink.menu` and `link` (the latter's

### 59.83 The one match: scope, checkpoint and implementation (§70.11)

Continued on 2026-11-18 after the completed sweep of §59.82. Read
§70.2, §70.8–§70.13; this is **the first text only**. Alec subsequently
authorized frequent local commits, particularly after runs. The completed
source and item-1.8 specification of §59.82 were checkpointed locally as
**`08d1cab2bf765a96173bd05f75b9a30aba57172e`**,
`Checkpoint item 1.8 tree-first comprehension and field reads`.
Its source snapshot is exactly §59.82's
`a6d71b77b3481131db0e313db3ac604172b3b3616c8e05e36460f92274e18815`
(1,218 files). The source below is its diff. The separately edited
sigma/pi plan, todo and item-1.5/item-1.6 plans are outside this checkpoint
and this change. No receipt or ignored data is committed. No push is made.

**One numerical function.** The default module name is built:
`bin/ConceptualMatch.py`, public function
`match(content, candidates, *, codebook=None, lane=None)`. Its nested
`ratios` calculation is the provisional measure of §70.12, not a new
metric: sum of coordinate-wise minima, divided independently by candidate
mass and content mass, with zero for a zero denominator. The smaller
operand width bounds the comparison, as before. It chooses no candidate,
sets no order threshold and detaches no operand.

The function owns the three coordinate cases. Without a codebook form
layout it compares the full point. With that layout, reference matching
zeros the coordinates before `percept_event_width`; forms with no meaning
therefore compare nothing. Zeroing preserves the previous reduction width
and coordinate addresses, including narrowed rows. `lane=0/1` is the field
reader's two independent reads: a row with meaning uses its first meaning
block as its signless code against the requested input lane; a row without
meaning uses its form. The form read still uses positive/negative input
components as before. `FieldProjection.stimulate` can consequently take both
coverages from this function **without a value or gradient change**; its
order filter, percept-collection membership and upward closure stay put.
No lanes are netted. The measure remains provisional, as Alec requested;
no contrary finding arose in these equality checks, which do not establish
that the measure is the final desired one.

| File and function | Change; other responsibilities retained |
| --- | --- |
| `ConceptualMatch.match` | Owns the numerical coverage and all three coordinate selections above. |
| `Memory.STMChunks.bind_menu` | Calls `match`; deletes `meaning_start`, `percept_band` and the menu's hand-cut location/time mask. Candidate addresses, exclusions, order eligibility and dummy stay. |
| `Memory.STMChunks.identity_sources` / `refresh` | Extracts refresh's existing off-stack identity/timeline lookup unchanged, including its preference for a SYMBOL or IDENTITY_REF reader. Both refresh and the word-object read use it. Refresh keeps its original read/activity writes; merely enumerating the menu makes none. |
| `Memory.MediumTermMemory.merge` | Replaces its whole-point containment read with `match(left, right)`. Its collection contract and merge writes stay. |
| `ReferenceClose.score` / `score_order` / `bind_site` | The percept flag replaces the old coordinate-reader callback; matching goes through `match`. Native candidate content stays distinct from its coordinate view used by exclusions, prime, continuity and other policy features. The form feature also gives the matcher its candidate content, rather than pre-cutting it for that match. |
| `ReferenceClose.individuals` | Keeps the original observed point transiently as `match_value` for partition/reconciliation coverage. The existing `content` still supplies exclusion tests, support, folding and returned descriptions; no durable sidecar is added. |
| `MemoryLink.menu` / `link` | Both containment tests call `match` on their native inputs. The menu retains carrier validation and the policy's coordinate-valued predicate; these are not the coverage operands. Its legal record passes native candidate content to the scorer. Existing link costs, collection restrictions and writes stay. |
| `FieldProjection.stimulate` | Two calls, one for each lane, replace its four local sliced coverage calls. |
| `ReferenceContext.bind_content` / `prepare_operands` | The menu receives the staged object's activated value and order for a raw word; the operator still receives the original word operand and its reference/order. A phrase keeps its current vector. |
| `Language.LanguageSpace.choose_operation` | Passes the journal's word source and the existing staged word reader to `prepare_operands`; deletes construction/passing of the old occurrence-band mask. Reads this additional staging context only if the grammar has bind. No selected action or chooser score is overridden. |

**Whole points preserved, by reader.** `MediumTermMemory.merge` keeps the
whole vectors for state, event and percept collections. `MemoryLink.menu`
and `link` keep the whole point for `kind='percept'`; ordinary reference,
state and event reads still use the owner's conceptual layout. A percept
read through `ReferenceClose.score_order` keeps its whole point, including
the form-feature read; explicit `percept_collections` still obtain their
primary membership from `PerceptCollections.read_collection`, not coverage
of their bounds. `FieldProjection`'s no-meaning fallback compares its whole
form/event block, just as before. A bank with no form layout also keeps the
whole supplied point. No new codec comparison of event places or times is
introduced.

The other uses of `IdentityRows.coordinates` remain where §70.11 leaves

nor `content_operand`/`remember_content` are redirected in this text. The
graded readers, cosine/key readers, recall, between-order matching and MTM

a fresh comprehension choice. Missing object rows supply no content offer.

neither STM nor MTM.

read. This is the implementation distinction used for the census below;

### 59.85 One-stream menu census and the deferred phrase evaluation

From **one final run** of the required native files, counting active
batch/mention sites and non-dummy candidates after native order eligibility:

| Mention | Menu calls | Staged object found | Object held off stack | Candidates on the word/current read | Candidates on the object/as implemented |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Raw single word | 144 | 100 | 66 | 15 | 32 |
| Phrase | 289 | not looked up | not looked up | 11 | 11 |

Thus **34** word calls value an available object by the leaf law without a
held identity; **44** have no staged object. Six direct `STMChunks.bind_menu`
unit-test calls have no word/phrase journal and are recorded separately,
not called words or phrases. Offers count candidate occurrences per menu,
not distinct identities across the run. Word and object alternatives use
the **same call's state and random stream**; the passive counter performs
no selection and makes no STM read/activity write.

The earlier required run, before the final cleanup that passes native
candidate content to the scorer's form-feature match, also passed all 95
cases (**54.16 s**). Its independent stream gave words **129/98/65/7/39**
(calls/found/held/word offers/object offers), and phrases **208**, **11/11**
offers. Both runs are recorded: their aggregate difference is not an
estimated effect of that value-preserving cleanup. As §70.10 reports, free
training draws change the number of menus. That section used eleven files
and different counts; its **198** single-word calls and **123** held objects
are not a like-for-like denominator for this five-file-plus-gate census.
Within each run, phrases are unchanged and the alternatives share inputs.

**What an object-valued phrase at the menu would take — report only.**
The insertion point is after the current stack/identity refresh and before
`ReferenceContext.prepare_operands` asks `bind_menu` to compare the phrase.
The existing evaluator is `Comprehension.Evaluation`; `Extension.reading`
drives `leaf`, `operation`, `completed` and `finish` over the **completed**
program, once per scored path. The tensor walk does not yet have that host
program: `ChunkJournal.capture` builds it after the walk, reading the
recorded actions, references, physical operands, case selections, held
refresh/publication witnesses and initial held field. A prefix evaluation
would need an equivalent bounded prefix view of those records, the input
field/positions, and the current phrase node. A word's object selection at
that time could still differ from the later final comprehension selection.

It cannot simply call the present completed evaluator without separating
its effects. The evaluator writes its private leaf/id/order arrays, action
frames, cases, timeline, equality observations, extension/composition maps
and held-concept copy. `completed` feeds `ComprehensionClose`; `finish`
prepares the tree's working idea store and calls `PartClosing.stage`, then
retains arrival readings. These are real trial STM/closing preparations,
although they do not commit LTM or MTM. An intermediate menu evaluation
would need to return only its current concept vector and private held
state, without closing or publishing a kept sentence. Calling `leaf`'s
`referent` itself is a read: it does not open a token or read MTM.
The current `capture` does read MTM token handles, so using it inside the
compiled tensor forward would also violate the existing no-pool-access
contract tested above. This is a boundary/design cost, not only a matmul.

For a sentence with **A** recorded nodes and **P** phrase-menu sites, replay
from the start to each site costs the sum of the **P prefix lengths**, plus
the existing operator and extension costs at each replayed node. Its upper
bound is **P × A** node evaluations instead of one **A**-node comprehension
per scored path; when P grows with A this is quadratic. Each independent
replay also clones the initial held field (**K × D** values), and the
current frame implementation allocates/copies program-sized arrays
(in particular `frames.index_copy`), so actual memory traffic exceeds that
node-count bound. Repeated evaluator construction also repeats case and
reference reads. Keeping incremental object-valued state beside the tree
could avoid prefix replay, but would have to follow every transpose,
unary offset, refresh/publication witness, alternative path and rollback.
That is a new carried state, not built here. No invented timing is offered
for an implementation that does not exist. This text leaves phrase values,
closes, capacity and all chooser actions alone.

### 59.87 Scalar parthood: the shared measure (§70.17; Codex, 2026-11-18)

Built with the replay repair of §69. The starting production source is
`31b24db620`; the intervening commits change documentation. The scalar
kernel was a clipped cosine, which made the support of a part relation
symmetric and ignored the operands' sizes. `Layers.Ops._part_kernel`
now separates each signed operand into its positive and negative lanes

## 60. Part B, second text: the loop of looks (Claude, 2026-11-16)

§58 and §59 are kept for Codex's returns of §57.6 and §55.3. This text
starts from the source §59 returns ("the starting source" below).

It builds what Alec decided in §54.6 and §54.7 and confirmed in §55: one
chooser; every look perceived and conceptualized at its `.where`; at a
look the grammar's option to call `interpret`; `mint` out of the walk.
The words in quotation marks are his; a rule marked *default* is
Claude's.

### 60.1 The rules

**The loop.**

1. *One loop of looks for a sentence.* In
   `Models._run_sentence_word_bricks`, the perception of every word
   before composing, the walk finished before the first word
   (`SentenceNarrowing.for_restore`, `finish_narrowing`), the candidate
   field built from all the words, and the loop of `read_field` are
   replaced by one loop. A step of it is one step of the walk
   (`narrow_step`, one call of `attend`), and what follows from that
   step (rules 3 to 6) is done before the next.
2. *The first look is the whole sentence.* It is the open pass as it is
   (`FamiliarTier.open_sentence`): every word bracket read in parallel.
   The walk's own readings (`native_word_poles`, the keys, the open read
   in `stage_input`) stay as they are.
3. *Every look is perceived and conceptualized.* After a step, the
   bracket in force at the chosen slot is the look's `.where`
   (*default*). It is written where perception reads a look's scope
   (`_passback_scope_where`, which `ModelAttention.handoff` writes today
   once, after the walk), the native percepts inside it are read
   (`cs_read_memberships` at that extent), and the concepts of every
   order are given from them (`cs_forward_content`). This is done whether
   or not the look holds a word.
4. *A look's field is a further reading.* The fields of a sentence's
   looks are kept in order beside the sentence's own field
   (`_sentence_open_fields`), which keeps its shape; each has its
   `.where` and `.when` (*default:* a field of their own with one reading
   for each look, of `attentionBudget` readings at most).
5. *Attention has no act that accepts a word; at a look the grammar may
   call `interpret`* (amended by §60.4, by rule 5a of §68.74, and by
   rule 5b of §68.79: the call is made with probability
   `interpretBias`, which is set to 1, and the chooser decides only
   the remaining share). The
   acts of `attend` are `focus` (divide, descend and, by rule 5a, the
   look at a word), `unfocus` (rule 11) and the three field acts.
   `mint` goes and nothing takes its place among them (`MintLayer`, its
   rule in `data/complete.grammar`, `GrammarPhases.EXAMINATION`). After a
   look is perceived and conceptualized, and before `attend` is called
   again, the grammar has its option: where the look is one word read
   with one lane (the test `narrowing_mask` made for a mint), it may call
   `interpret` on that word. *Default:* the grammar's own chooser decides
   it as it decides its other one-operand rules (`score_unary`,
   `interpret` against abstaining), and the decision is recorded,
   explored and credited as its other choices are. A word read with both
   lanes is not offered. A bracket whose word was interpreted is done, as
   an accepted one is today.
6. *`interpret` finds the word, and the word joins the tree.* When it is
   taken, the word is found (*default:* from the sentence's staged bank,
   which stays where it is staged; moving the lookup itself to the look
   is not in this text), and if it is found its brick runs then
   (`forecast_percept`, `perceive`, `symbolize`, `observe_percept`) and
   `word_step` deposits the word (§55.1, rule 1) and composes. A word
   never interpreted has no brick, is not composed and is no leaf.
   *Default:* a word's brick and its forecast are made once, by the
   first path that finds it, and the other paths reuse them.
7. *The word forecast is made at the look.* `stage_expectation` no longer
   forecasts a sentence's words once: `WordExpectation.word_distribution`
   is taken one arrival at a time, in the order the words are found, each
   forecast made before its word's brick. Its results keep their places
   by word (`_word_expectation`, `_word_column`,
   `_word_expectation_mask`) and its cost keeps its name.

**One chooser.**

8. *`CandidateAttention` goes,* with `SentenceField.place`, the choice
   and the alternative in `FieldTraversal.select`, the departure in the
   candidate's choice (`candidates` of `SentenceCredit.departure`, the
   cost `attention.candidate_departure`), and the field's own allowance.
   `SentenceField` stays as the record of the words placed: it takes a
   word when the word is interpreted, and keeps `remember`,
   `placements`, `full_admission`, `grammar_leaves`, `source_order`,
   `ordered_reconstruction` and `report`.
9. *`attend` reads what has been understood.* It is given what
   `ModelCandidateAttention.context` assembles without the candidates'
   own support: STM and its slots' places, the gist, the open request,
   priming, the expectation's prime and the residual of the percept
   forecast. *Default:* through one linear map to the chooser's width,
   added to each bracket's key, started at zero from a private generator,
   so that before any teaching `attend` scores as it does on the
   starting source.
10. *The allowance belongs to the presentation.* It is `attentionBudget`
    for each sentence of the presentation, held by one meter (*default*).
    The bracket table keeps its size for a sentence.
11. *`unfocus`.* It puts back the bracket that the last `focus` of this
    walk divided or entered, costs one act, and is legal while such a
    focus is in force and none of its words has been interpreted
    (*default*). *Default:* it takes the address `mint` had, so the menu
    keeps six acts and `bracket_anchor` its size; that row starts again
    at zero.
12. *Paths.* A path that departs in the walk takes the same looks, the
    same calls of `interpret` and the same word steps up to its
    departure, and its own after it. The kept path replays its recorded
    steps.

**The teacher.**

13. *The reading lesson teaches `attend`* (assessment §9.2, with `mint`
    gone). While `AttentionLesson.reading_lesson` is set and the model
    trains, the lesson names the first word not yet interpreted. For
    `attend` the target of a step is the legal `focus` that reaches that
    word by the fewest acts; no field act and no `unfocus` is a target.
    For the grammar the target at a look is `interpret` where the look is
    that word, and abstaining at any other look. Each target is the
    choice taken, and its cost is the cross entropy of the chooser's
    probability of it, booked as `attention.reading_lesson` is today. If
    `interpret` can never be offered on a named word (both lanes), the
    lesson passes over that word and reports it.

**Removed with these.**

14. The draws that `finish_narrowing` makes and discards; and
    `_captured_narrowing`, `advance_narrowing` and `narrowing_stable` if
    the loop no longer calls them.
15. The search of the surface for each word's bytes in `stage_input`:
    the spans come from the stem's offsets (`_ar_word_part_offsets`). If
    a path has no offsets, stop and say which.

**The name.**

16. *`mint` is renamed `interpret` wherever it does not create* (Alec,
    §60.5). Every occurrence of the word, in `bin/`, `test/`, `data/`
    and `doc/*.md`, that names the processing of a word at a look (the
    act that was `mint` and before it `gloss`, its tests, reports and
    comments, and "minted" said of a word that reached the grammar)
    becomes `interpret` or "interpreted". An occurrence that names the
    making of a concept, an object, a row, an identity or a referent
    stays (`_mint_row`, `concept_mint_count`, `mint_threshold`, a close
    request whose mode makes a referent, and the like). The plans and
    benchmarks under `doc/` are records and are not edited.

**Not changed in this text.** `Examination.run` (an input with no words
to compose) keeps its whole walk at once. `InterpretLayer.mandatory`
keeps its value, since it also rules the leaf's inverse in generation and
the closing of references. `Attention.narrowing_mask`'s tests stay,
apart from the name of what they allow. A span of several words taken as
one unit is not built. Part A's remainder is not built: `expect` at each
look, the surprise given to `attend`, and the prior
(`BracketKeys._codebook_retrieval_prior`), which stays.

### 60.2 Certificates

1. *The first word is composed before the walk is finished.* On a
   sentence of three known words, the first `word_step` follows fewer
   calls of `attend` than the walk takes in all. Fails on the starting
   source.
2. *Every look has a field.* A sentence's look fields are as many as its
   first look and its steps, each with its bracket's `.where`; a step
   that finds no word has one; `_passback_scope_where` holds each look's
   interval when its perception runs.
3. *Only interpreted words are composed.* A word never interpreted has
   no brick call, no `word_step` and is no leaf; a word interpreted has
   each once in a path.
4. *The grammar's option is where `mint` was legal.* It is offered at a
   look of one word read with one lane, and at no other; no act of
   `attend` accepts a word; `MintLayer` and the rule `mint` are in no
   menu, no source file and no grammar file.
5. *One chooser.* No source file names `CandidateAttention`; a
   checkpoint that holds its weights loads, with those weights retired
   and named.
6. *The same acts give the same sentence.* With the map of rule 9 at
   zero, and the starting source and this one both made to take the same
   acts on a sentence, reading its words in the order of the text, the
   kept tree, the meaning and the row written to LTM are equal (atol
   1e-6). If they differ, the first value that differs is reported with
   its producer.
7. *The word forecast is causal in the order found.* The forecast for a
   word reads only the words found before it; for words found in the
   order of the text it equals the starting source's.
8. *The allowance.* In a packed row of four sentences the last sentence
   takes looks, where the starting source leaves it none.
9. *`unfocus`.* After a focus, `unfocus` restores the bracket table to
   what it was, costs one act, and is not legal once a word of the
   focused bracket is interpreted. The menu of `attend` has six acts.
10. *A departure replays.* A path departing at step s has the same
    looks, interpretations and word steps as the first path before s.
11. *The lesson's targets read every word in order,* in the fewest acts,
    on sentences of one to six words; a taught step books the cross
    entropy of its target; a test fails without the teacher.
12. Both stopping gates pass.

### 61.2 A path without the offsets (§60.1, rule 15)

The existing
`test_word_admission.py::test_29_each_reading_publishes_only_its_words[MM_text.xml]`
uses `reading_fixtures.field_text_config(examine=False)`: the parallel
field-only read, with `intersection`, `union` and `not`. A passive
observer of `ModelAttention.stage_input` finds actual word surfaces,
an active shape **(4,8)**, and **no `_ar_word_part_offsets`**. The
reader therefore uses the surface-byte search that rule 15 removes.
This path has no attention walk. The other two parameters, MM_grammar
and XOR_grammar, have offsets of shapes **(4,8,13)** and **(4,6,13)**
and have a walk. All three existing assertions pass (**3 passed in
4.91 s**); none is changed.

The producer is `PartSpace._embed_radix`, the whole-slab branch in
`bin/Spaces.py`. It already calculates `_wspans` with
`Meronomy.percept_spans(_raw)` and uses those exact intervals to make
`word_texts_2d` and assign each emitted part to its word group. It
does not retain the word-axis intervals. `InputSpace.finalize_stem`
therefore has no word-axis offsets to hand to attention; its retained
part spans are on the different, emitted-part axis. The serial radix
and ladder branches do retain their word offsets.

**For Alec and Claude.** Rule 15 explicitly says to stop and name a
path that has no offsets. I recommend retaining this whole-slab stem's
already-computed word intervals and passing them to the common
attention staging reader, so the surface search can be deleted for
every path. This adds no parsing rule and changes no fixture capacity;
the producer already knows the intervals. May this producer port be
built, or should the parallel field-only path cease staging word
brackets? The latter also needs an explicit disposition for its current
staged word/gist read. No replacement or bypass is built pending this
answer. §69's independent fixed curricula continue unchanged.

Claude's subsequent §68.69 independently confirms this producer and
recommends retaining its intervals. It requires a distinct name for
them: supplying `_ar_word_part_offsets` on the whole-slab path would
incorrectly tell other readers that it is word-major. That section
explicitly awaits Alec's word. No loop change is built while it waits.

### 61.4 Readers and the two byte frames (§68.73 B.5)

Every source reader of `_ar_word_part_offsets` was checked:

| File and function | Read retained |
|---|---|
| `Models._stage_fixed_residual_part_capacity` | Pads the same word-major part axis; retains offsets |
| `Models._stage_reading_grammar_references` | Its presence selects word-major matching; compares the first part offset with a grammar word's byte start |
| `Models._stage_serial_concept_rows` | Gives starts to `WholeSpace.stage_word_primitives`; encodes word occurrence `.where` |
| `Models._run_batch_once` | Marks the word-major part dimension dynamic |
| `Models._run_aligned_word_chunk_loop` | Stages/chunks the part-offset tensor with ids and masks |
| `Models._tensor_peer_while_ready` | Requires the tensor for the canonical word-major body |
| `Models._run_tensor_peer_word_pipeline` | Passes the local offsets into the perceptual word body |
| `InputSpace.word_part_offsets_at`, read by `Models._per_word_body_step` | Returns a word's offsets to `present_word` and the native perceptual read |
| `bench_train_word_bucket._profile_peer_legs` | Supplies the first word's offsets to the profiled body |
| `ModelAttention.stage_input` | Replaced by `word_intervals`; no longer reads the part-offset tensor |

`InputSpace.Start` and `Reset` clear that tensor, and
`_finalize_serial_word_stem` publishes it. Those writers are unchanged.
The targeted census observes **48 calls**. Exactly three have no offsets,
all on a whole-slab text stem and **none running a walk**:
`test_29_each_reading_publishes_only_its_words[MM_text.xml]` and the two
new `test_whole_slab_keeps_repeated_and_cut_word_intervals` parameters.
This is the census of tests run, not of the default tier. The incidental
ordinal-slot key issue of §68.70 is unchanged.

The word-major offsets are in the concatenated **host-token byte frame**.
`InputSpace._lex_batch` constructs `_analyse_surfaces` after removing every
NUL byte, and `_lex_and_embed` passes those strings to the stem. Thus a
raw staged `[0, 1]` can have a host surface `[1]`: offset zero in the
stem, position one in `_staged_concepts_in`. This explains Claude's
record without changing either frame. No mismatch occurred in the 48
calls above. The cross-frame readers are `ModelAttention.native_word_poles`
(its brackets/native part spans against the raw whole-property field),
`FamiliarTier.open_sentence` (same), and
`Models._stage_reading_word_concepts` with
`_stage_reading_grammar_references` (raw-surface word intervals matched to
native extents/offsets). Kept sentence `word_extents` also retain the
attention intervals for raw reconstruction readers. The port does not
repair these pre-existing frame differences.

### 61.6 Stop: a pure sibling has no act that looks at it

**Producer.** `Attention.narrowing_mask` returns `[False, False, True]`
for a known, pure single-word bracket: neither divide nor descend is
legal; only the old attention acceptance is. `narrow_step` also makes
all three field operations illegal on that pure singleton. Removing
acceptance leaves no act by which attention selects that bracket. The
new grammar option is offered only at the current look, as rule 5 says.
The unselected right sibling of a split has not been that look.

**Native reproduction.** Three words, `red cat sleeps`, are admitted by
the existing training-form admission, with no teaching or changed seed,
capacity, rate or budget. The unchanged exploration configuration has
attentionBudget **32**. Their native lanes are each **(1,0)**. Force the
legal focuses in source order and take every offered interpretation:

| Look | Attention act / post-act bracket | Grammar option |
|---|---|---|
| First | Whole input, bytes 0 to 14 | Not one word |
| Second | Focus at slot 0, action 1; bytes 0 to 3 | Interprets `red` |
| Third | Focus at slot 1, action 7; bytes 4 to 7 | Interprets `cat` |
| Next needed | Right sibling, slot 2, bytes 8 to 14 | Never looked at; no legal attention act |

The final table has three brackets `[0,3]`, `[4,7]`, `[8,14]`, done
`[True, True, False]`, **2 acts spent, 30 left**, and all six attention
acts false on the remaining bracket. Only word positions **0 and 2**
get a brick and `word_step`; position **4** gets neither. If the first
interpretation abstains, only position **2** is read: the first and last
pure brackets both lack a next look. The grammar never declines an
offer on the final word; the offer cannot be reached.

This also reproduces on the **returned pre-loop source**, independently
of the prototype: its five progress actions are **1, 2, 7, 8, 14** and
all three words are accepted. At the last step its slot-2 legal menu is
`[False,False,True,False,False,False]`. The local requirement test deletes
only the retired acceptance column and asserts that some attention look
remains: **1 failed in 0.96 seconds**, because none does. Thus the missing
act is not an error in the new per-look field or forecast implementation.

The not-yet-built `unfocus` does not resolve this example under rule 11:
the last focus has already interpreted its left word, so reversal is
illegal. Nor can the teacher of rule 13 use a Boolean field operation:
its targets are focuses only, and no field act is legal on this bracket
in any case. Certificate 11 cannot reach its one-to-six-word requirement
under the literal mask.

**For Alec and Claude.** May `focus` select a live, uninterpreted word
bracket **at the same level**, even when its reading is already pure?
Recommended: this spends one attention act and perceives the selected
interval; it does not descend below a known word and does not accept it.
Then grammar alone may interpret or abstain. It can use focus's existing
act address, keeping the six-act menu. No automatic scan of sibling
words or automatic interpretation is proposed.

This needs an amendment to the statement in §60.1 that the
`narrowing_mask` tests stay apart from the name, and to the exact meaning
of focus on a word bracket. §60.3 step 3 requires stopping where the
default cannot be built as written; no new legality has been installed.
The teacher's target would remain the fewest legal focuses, including
this one final look. Awaiting Alec's decision.

### 61.9 A checkpoint can remember the old acceptance and interpretation separately

The first difference in this run of the fixed comparison occurs at
construction and load, before the first sentence. In the saved §61.1
state, each placement column has shape **4,195 × 16**. The construction
with the old field declaration removed has **4,192 × 16**.
`PartsOfSpeech.order_reservations` counts two order-one concepts for
the formal input and output and an order-two concept for the operator.
Removing that declaration changes the blocks from **2,346 / 1,239 /
610** to **2,346 / 1,237 / 609**. The raw state loader rejects the
shape. Consequently §61.5's preliminary exact comparisons cannot be
reported as certificate 6 on this source.

The ordinary checkpoint route reproduces a semantic problem even
without the raw-state comparison. On archived `367950675f` with
`explore-1.xml`, the native IDs were 46 and 47 for the two acceptance
arguments and 98 for its operator. The interpretation arguments were
35 and 36, and its operator was 93. Starting with the original construction
stream, I wrote a relation from 98 to 93 at trust +0.75 through
`append_relation`, then saved and reloaded it. It was LTM1 row 125.
The old loader returned true. The new `load_weights` reaches
`GrammarConceptCheckpoint.prepare` and refuses the removed declarations
with “removed argument concepts require an explicit identity migration”.

In a second old checkpoint I allocated the remaining **583** order-two
concepts through `new_concept(order=2)` and gave each a relation to 93.
The old loader restored all **610/610** occupied seats and the distinct
98 → 93 endpoints of row 125 with positive evidence **0.75**. The new
loader refused this checkpoint too. These are diagnostic writes in
local checkpoints on the existing capacities. Adding a fresh primitive
in place of the retired declaration can restore the number of seats,
but a full block cannot house both a new concept and every saved one.
Renaming 98 to the existing interpretation would turn the example
relation into a self-relation. Reusing 98 for unfocus would make a saved
claim about acceptance into one about undoing a focus.

**Decision for Alec and Claude under §73.** Certificate 5 calls for
loading an older checkpoint and §68.75 fixes capacity. I recommend
preserving the former operator and its two formal arguments as ordinary
historical concepts when their identities and learned records fit,
retiring their executable declarations. For a checkpoint where they
cannot fit alongside the live grammar, I recommend rejecting it with
the affected order and capacity before applying the load. This requires
an explicit exception for the full checkpoint. No migration has been
chosen or applied.

### 61.12 Regeneration decision and the loop through unfocus

Alec accepted regeneration with new baselines. The comparison preserves the original
measurements in §61.11. Loading the regenerated model again and restoring the
same reading random states reproduced **4/4** trees, meaning tensors, stored
rows, forecast tensors and word masks exactly. Superseded grammar models can
be regenerated from their recipes. This decision supersedes the proposed
migration of the hypothetical full block in §61.9.

Certificate 10 exposed an index past the end of a three-act reference walk
when the alternative declined the second interpretation. Its cause was a
variable-length action carrier used as if it spanned the allowance. Completed
walks now pad their histories, without taking actions. A departure in the
grammar replays the attention act that reached its word. The two paths in the
test agree on all looks through that act and differ on the selected grammar
decision. The two stopping tests passed in the same run (**7 passed, 7.11 s**).

The candidate scorer, its feature assembler and its separate traversal have
been removed. The bracket chooser reads the prefix through the zero-initialized
linear map in `AttentionContext`. The checkpoint reader names and discards
the former scorer weights. The optimizer round-trip, loop, path-credit and
stopping tests gave **39 passed, 28.58 s**.

A presentation now gives each stream one allowance sized from its number
of present sentences. In certificate 8 four two-word sentences used one
eight-act meter; each sentence took two acts with a two-slot table. The
fourth began with six spent and finished with eight spent. Certificate 9
found that address 2 was illegal after a split before unfocus was implemented.
It now restores that split's original parent and removes its child. A pure
word look records no undo frame. Interpreting an enclosed word bars undo.
The new tests, the earlier loop cases and both stopping tests gave **9
passed, 6.44 s**. The complete examination reader still has a fullgraph
implementation. The sentence loop no longer uses look-ahead for a stable
word, and padding an exhausted examination consumes no random draw.

### 61.13 The reading teacher and the regenerated comparison

Alec approved rebuilding old training baselines from their recipes. On the completed attention menu I rebuilt the four-sentence comparison of §61.1 from its original construction and reading streams. The regenerated model loaded into a fresh instance. The second read reproduced every recorded field exactly, including choices, trees, meaning slots and roots, memory rows and forecasts. The comparison against the *original* source also recovered exact equality for all four trees, all four meaning roots, all 15 stored rows (4, 4, 4, 3) and all ten forecast components at all 16 interpreted places. The differences on the intermediate build in §61.11 are superseded by this measurement. Before, each sentence took nine calls of `attend`. Now each takes four. The original predictor also computed a distribution, prediction, omission and activation at padding. On this loop those four arrays have zeros at places where no word arrived. The word masks agree exactly.

For certificate 11 the native teacher previously delivered zero words on every length from one to six. All six tests failed. `AttentionLesson.ReadingTargets` now resolves the named occurrences against the native word places, skips and reports those held on both lanes, and chooses the shortest legal focus to the next named occurrence. The calculation shares the walk's actual cuts. A split can put its left child under the current look immediately. `Looks.run` teaches the bracket choice and the grammar choice at their own logits. The lesson books the mean cross entropy per taught decision on the first path. Evaluation reads freely. The six lengths all passed with **0, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6** calls of `attend`, positive lesson cost and a gradient at the scorer. In the native two-word training test both streams read places **0 then 1**, the chooser parameter moved, and the attention projection had exactly the reconstruction writer. Empty masks previously attached a spurious answer gradient. The score-function reader now includes the attention probabilities only when a departure actually took one.

`WordForecast.begin_path` starts each path at the same pre-arrival predictor state. A later path reuses each previously made forecast and advances its own prefix on that arrival. Forecasting a newly discovered word therefore reads the words its path has already interpreted. The assessment observes the native bracket mask, actual chooser calls, selected extents and grammar decisions. Its probes restore the hooks after reading. The field and curriculum observers now report the actual interpreted place, stream mask, charged bracket work and the taught cross entropy. For the percept census the observer reads the native whole-property result and the basic-percept result inside each real opening or selected look and counts distinct keys positive on both lanes. On the fixed-action four-sentence check all **16 opening word extents** and **16 subsequent selected extents** had zero of each. The 160-sentence measurement is separate.

The checkpoint reader warns with each retired candidate-scorer key. Since action address 2 changed meaning, a saved acceptance anchor and its optimizer moments are cleared there. The five other anchors are retained. A checkpoint whose learned grammar identities cannot be aligned reports the removed declarations and asks for regeneration. The strengthened test starts the six saved anchor rows at 0.375 and checks the one cleared row and the five preserved rows.

The teacher, checkpoint migration, replay and stopping tests in `test_native_candidate_attention.py` (checkpoint case), `test_reading_curriculum.py`, `test_loop_of_looks.py`, `test_whole_path_repairs.py` and the two stopping-gate files gave **36 passed in 20.64 s**. The stepped observer, handoff, assessment and shared-meter tests in `test_attention_thinking_steps.py`, `test_attention_thinking_handoff.py`, `test_assessment.py` and `test_one_attention.py` (meter case) gave **19 passed in 31.41 s**. The field-only and composing versions of the word-forecast test gave **2 passed in 5.67 s**. The field-only model retains its original dimensions and normalized distribution. Its mask and loss are zero. The composing fixture tests normalization at arrivals and nonzero predictor gradients. Each model still uses the test's four input strings.

### 61.14 The declaration of interpretation on the verbal configurations

Before the port the native verbal XOR walk had **124 pure-word opportunities, zero offers, zero interpretations and zero bricks** on its four inputs. The isolated pure-word logits were **0 and minus infinity**. `OperationSelectionLayer.choose_interpret` found no declared unary on this model. Its old grammar had admitted words with the attention act. A temporary grammar with one added compose rule gave the chooser a legal option and raised its fixed grammar reservation by two order-one seats and one order-two seat. Alec decided to declare the operation and reserve those seats on grammars that compose words.

I read all 15 affected production grammars through the actual loader, including its interpretation of the older inline XML rules. Ten needed the new declaration. The counts below are the fixed grammar seats at orders one and two. These are in addition to the configured concept pool.

| Grammar | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| MM_sequence_predict.xml | 17, 7 | 19, 8 |
| MM_shamatha.xml | 23, 10 | 25, 11 |
| MM_xor_loopback.xml | 16, 7 | 18, 8 |
| POS_smoke.xml | 31, 12 | 33, 13 |
| RamsifiedModel.xml | 33, 13 | 35, 14 |
| XOR_grammar.xml | 16, 7 | 18, 8 |
| ladder.grammar | 61, 22 | 63, 23 |
| shamatha.grammar | 33, 12 | 35, 13 |
| tied_reconstruction_output_benchmark.grammar | 56, 20 | 58, 21 |
| xor.grammar | 16, 7 | 18, 8 |

`complete.grammar` and `default.grammar` already declared the operation. The loader places `examination.grammar`, `MM_text_fixture.xml` and `MM_ltm_consolidation_fixture.xml` on the examination-only path. Their operator sets and reservations are unchanged. All ten ports use the ordinary declaration and existing allocator. On verbal XOR the constructed blocks are now **11, 23, 10**. The same four inputs produced **124 pure opportunities and 124 offers**. The fresh free chooser abstained every time. The isolated logits were **0 and −1**. Making a word available and learning to choose it are separate measurements.

The added verbal-XOR mechanism test first failed with eligibility **[false, false]** for a pure and an ineligible place. It now gets **[true, false]**. Those assertions and both stopping gates gave **3 passed in 4.30 s**. The first verbal-proof setup subsequently exposed a second producer. A compose-only grammar derives its generate catalogue. That builder included mandatory lexical naming as a structural unary, then called its inverse with only a point. The native reader requires the terminal's word bank. Grammars with an explicit generate catalogue already omit mandatory operations from that menu. I applied the same declared property to the implicit catalogue, on my recommendation under §73. The expanded test saw `interpret` in the structural unary menu before the repair and passed in **3.35 s** after it. The Boolean binary operations remain available. Lexical naming keeps its existing terminal reader.

### 61.19 Reading curriculum and its control

Each stage ran its original 64 presentations of four streams, in curriculum order, with the same Adam setting 0.01. The enabled model’s two-word reading changed from zero exact grammar readbacks to four. Its four-word reading already had four exact readbacks on entry and kept all four. The stage also requires final lesson cross entropy at most 0.01 per row and a strict decrease of its sum since the first presentation. This last condition failed on reading_four.

| Mode | Stage | Grammar readbacks | Free readbacks | Sum of first → last CE | Stage | Seconds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| disabled | reading_two | 4/4 → 4/4 | 4/4 → 4/4 | 4.01350403 → 0.0204261267 | pass | 195.606 |
| disabled | reading_four | 4/4 → 4/4 | 4/4 → 4/4 | 0.0170679577 → 0.00151605823 | pass | 393.763 |
| enabled | reading_two | 0/4 → 4/4 | 4/4 → 4/4 | 4.0127666 → 2.61063956e-05 | pass | 197.805 |
| enabled | reading_four | 4/4 → 4/4 | 4/4 → 4/4 | 4.01728422e-05 → 0.000587228817 | fail | 635.048 |

Final enabled per-row CE was **0.000000477, 0.000008523, 0.000008553, 0.000008553** on two words and **0.000146822, 0.000148089, 0.000145973, 0.000146345** on four. Both stages were interpretable against their passing controls. Each had zero attempted or kept departures. In the preparatory stages, identity permanence failed in both modes. Identifying words passed in the disabled control and failed in the enabled model. The curriculum’s whole-checkout start/end signature differed while other grammars and test ports were being completed. Both models used their generated point-only grammar with explicit generation throughout. The receipt is retained as run.

Each interpreted word has exactly one brick, word step and leaf per path, and an unproductive look still has a scoped field. |
| 4. Grammar owns interpretation | Passed on “red cat sleeps” and on the pure/ineligible pair in verbal XOR. Forcing only the legal focuses and the offered grammar decisions gives all three bricks. A look alone admits no word. The ten grammar reservations and proof-setup regression are recorded in §61.14. |

Forecasts are scattered back to their own native places. The four unused padding components that changed are recorded in §61.13. |
| 8–9. Presentation allowance and unfocus | Four two-word sentences used two acts apiece from one eight-act meter. The fourth started with six spent. Undo restores the parent and costs one act, and is illegal after interpretation inside that parent. The menu has six addresses. |
| 10. Replay | Passed for a departure in interpretation and a departure in the bracket walk. The prefix compares the actual looks and interpreted places, including the focus that reached a departing grammar decision. |

The native loss reaches the taught chooser parameters and an ineligible word is reported. Free learning is reported in §61.19. |
| 12. Stopping gates | The numerical XOR convergence test and raised-class denotation test both passed after the final grammar change. The last run with the forced reconstruction certificate gave **3 passed in 44.14 s**. |

**Defaults built.** The selected slot supplies the look interval. The sentence keeps its open field and ordered further fields. There can be one opening plus `attentionBudget` charged looks, so the opening is additional to the default’s count of charged readings. The unary scorer decides interpretation against abstaining, and the native staged bank supplies the word. Paths reuse a word’s first forecast and brick, and advance their own causal prefixes. The detached prefix enters attention through a zero-initialized linear projection. One presentation meter supplies the declared per-sentence allowance. Unfocus reverses the last retained division or entry while none of its words has been interpreted. It occupies address 2 and starts with a zero anchor. Repeated unchanged looks are legal and are bounded by the allowance. Their cost and the frequency of abstention are visible in §§61.17–61.18.

**Two forced downstream fixtures.** In `test_operators_final_b.py::test_both_training_trials_share_bootstrap_snapshot`, the untrained reader could abstain throughout. The assertion that the bootstrap had actual word witnesses then found an empty context audit. The fixture now executes its word arrivals in source order through the native chooser before comparing snapshots. It passed in **159.29 s**. In `test_forced_not_and_or_descend_and_snapshot_certificate`, the prescribed field operations no longer accepted a word. The test previously recovered **0/4** multisets. Its forced reading now takes a legal grammar interpretation and leaves unfocus out of its prescribed forward sequence. Both reads recover **4/4** and the same four zero residuals. The native reconstruction-cost, content-cost, spelling, and snapshot assertions all pass. These ports run only inside the two tests.

**Verbal proof.** With the declared grammar, the original 400 epochs and 1,600 presentations completed. The independent field inverse recovered **4/4**: hello world, hello there, loving world and loving there. Numeric predictions were **0.5000, 0.5000, 0.5000, 0.5000** against **0, 1, 1, 0**, rounded MSE **0.25**. Final printed output loss was **0.1750** and reconstruction loss **0.0000**. The grammar proof **failed** its availability assertion. At least one of the four kept readings had an unavailable grammar inverse. The existing test exits at that assertion before printing the per-row grammar outputs, so the precise number of unavailable rows and the exact multiset count are unmeasured on this training run. The four printed word pairs are from the field inverse. At the producer, `reconstruct_grammar_sentence` marks an active row missing when generation is truncated or its text is empty or contains NUL. The free untrained trace in §61.14 establishes abstention on those inputs before training. It does not distinguish the three conditions on the trained rows. The test took **951.51 s**. §59.82 reported **4/4** grammar and **4/4** field, the same final losses and numeric predictions, and **594.765215 s**. This is a learning result under §43.

**Targeted testing.** The changed-test and loop group produced **72 passed, 4 skipped, 1 failed** before the bootstrap snapshot port above. The failed case then passed with the original assertion. The marked fixture assessment produced **31 passed, 2 skipped, 279 deselected in 357.32 s**. The eight applicable fixture readings were repeated with their passive native offer traces enabled, **8 passed in 236.48 s**. Each repeated source had the same rung status and failure reasons. The four-word curriculum’s summed-loss criterion and the verbal grammar availability check are the remaining measured learning failures, alongside the preparatory, ladder and lesson limitations in §§61.17–61.19. Both stopping gates and the loop mechanism certificates pass. §72 and §68.75 prescribe targeted tests here. The whole-item default sweep and the slow tier are outside this return.

### 61.22 The interpretation bias of §68.80

Before the change the unforced three-word certificate got zero bricks and word steps. The bracket walk offered the words, and the unary chooser preferred abstention. At the new default of one, the native walk interprets each of the three words once, with one brick and one word step per word, and finishes within the existing allowance. The rule applies to training and evaluation. It requires the existing grammar declaration and native offer.

`OperationSelectionLayer.interpret_at_look` reads the model’s configured `architecture.interpretBias`. At intermediate values it draws once per offered stream from the existing PyTorch generator on the word tensor’s device. Presentation snapshots already capture that generator. Replay keeps the drawn branch as well as the action, and an interpretation departure stays on the learned branch. A direct call has probability one, zero alternatives and no score-function or grammar-lesson gradient. The independent attention lesson still charges its own focuses. Zero and one consume no bias draws. The parameter is range-checked at construction and declared in the XML schema and parameter reference.

The fresh-reader, zero-bias equivalence and supplied-uniform tests failed before and passed after. Tests at both endpoints check the random stream. The partial-bias test observes which rows actually called the scorer, tests the equality threshold and replays the saved branches. The shortest-path lesson checks lengths one through six at both settings. At bias one its sole one-word opening books no target. At bias zero it still trains the unary anchors. In `test_loop_of_looks.py`, the selective first-word abstention and interpretation-departure tests explicitly select the learned share. In `test_native_attention_field.py` the reversed reading explicitly does the same for its prescribed first refusal. Their original selection, prefix, gradient and admission assertions remain. The three-look test of a declined bracket is unchanged.

The bias, loop, reading lesson, native attention field, assessment, and two stopping-gate files gave **50 passed in 27.42 seconds**. The invalid negative, above-one and NaN construction cases plus the final reversed reading and bias cases gave **7 passed in 6.71 seconds**. There was no change to capacity, work allowance or presentation count.

### 61.24 The definitions in certificate 82 and the fixture readings

At bias one the fixtures produced **6 passes, 2 failures and 23 unavailable** on rung one. In §61.18 all eight applicable fixtures failed. In §59.82 seven passed and certificate 84 failed. The full per-source comparison, including the trained lesson and the forecast measurements, is in §64.4. The bias assessment’s operator assertions gave **31 passed, 2 skipped, 279 deselected in 170.23 s**. The rung measures a trusted word–object definition as well as a word in the kept tree.

Both certificate 82 fixtures first read “alpha gamma” and then read it with gamma hidden. They supply no definition. For sigmaPi, the three one-word assessment probes each read alpha and found one trusted object, 111. For predictor, all three read alpha and found no object or definition evidence. In a diagnostic of the latter case the first presentation admitted neither word and the second admitted both. The diagnostic observed no definition before, during or after the probe.

The producer is the lexical occurrence count at the kept close. `FamiliarTier.commit_read_words` retains admitted lexical leaves, excluding an absent word and a leaf kept as a sign or a bare percept. `promote_candidates` requires three distinct retained occurrences within its horizon. `promote_identity` calls `InterpretLayer.define` on promotion. Tracing a separate native run, both maps retained one, then two, then three occurrences of alpha including the probe. The third produced a DEF with evidence (1, 0). Restoring the assessment trial restored the pre-probe inventory with no object. The two maps share this writer. The original bias measurement captured its field, tree and DEF evidence, but did not instrument each increment. The fixture’s two teaching reads do not guarantee the three retained occurrences. This accounts for the varying rung outcome without changing promotion, trust or the presentations.

The chooser-specific ports are `test_1_2_3_words_join_before_the_walk_finishes`, `test_10_interpret_departure_keeps_the_focus_that_reached_its_word` and `test_reversed_candidate_reads_keep_native_field_order_without_teacher`. Each formerly got a free first refusal on the fresh default. Each now sets bias zero for its original selective refusal or departure. `test_11_lesson_teaches_shortest_walk_and_interpretation` now checks its previous shortest-walk assertions at both endpoints and checks which branch books the grammar target. In the one-word case bias one interprets with no grammar target. The bias implementation is local commit `4e0db320f2`.

## 62. Part A's remainder: the forecast of a look and its surprise (Claude, 2026-11-16; a design, with one question for Alec)

§61 is kept for Codex's return of §60.3. This section starts from the
source §61 returns. It has no text for Codex yet: the text differs as a
whole by the answer to §62.5.

### 62.1 What exists after §60 (read in the source)

- *The percept forecast and the word forecast* are made when the grammar
  interprets a word, for that word's arrival (§60.1, rules 6 and 7):
  `PerceptExpectation.forecast`, from the mean and the last of earlier
  arrivals, and `WordExpectation.word_distribution`. Neither takes a
  place: each says what comes next.
- *`expect`* runs once, at the open pass (`ConceptSpread.open_prediction`).
  Its input is the observed field over the rows of order zero
  (`_observed_knowing`, the greatest of each lane over the glance's
  readings, `IntuitionField.observed`), and its output is the expected
  field over the same rows (`_expected_knowing`). Its teacher is
  omission: words hidden from the stem before perception, and the cost
  is the difference between what it expects from the lossy field and the
  field with them present (`Omission.concept_teacher`,
  `expectation.concepts`).
- *The prior of a bracket* (`BracketKeys._codebook_retrieval_prior`) is
  made once in `stage_input`: each word key's likeness to the codebook's
  rows, weighted by priming (`priming_weights`, which is one plus the
  expected field plus desire). `narrow_step` adds it to each bracket's
  score.

### 62.2 What remains of part A (§12.2, rules 1 to 3)

1. Each look forecasts what will be conceived over its bracket's whole
   span, then reads it; the difference is the look's surprise. Alec: "every
   time we look in a new place, we have an expectation about what we will
   perceive there, and what we will conceive about it", and "yes, we
   expect the whole .where span".
2. This takes the place of the prior.
3. The surprise is a signal to `attend` ("I would provide it surprise as a
   signal to the attention algorithm"); what `attend` does with it is
   learned.

### 62.3 The design (Claude's, for §62.5's first answer)

1. *A look's forecast is `expect` with the look's span left out.* Before
   the look is perceived, `expect` is taken on the observed field formed
   from the readings outside the look's bracket, and closed upward
   (`FieldProjection.close`). So it says what should be in this place,
   given what was seen elsewhere. The place enters by what is left out,
   which is the form omission already teaches, so `expect` needs no new
   input and no new teacher.
2. *The surprise is the difference, both ways.* With the look's field
   read at its extent (§60.1, rule 3) and the forecast, per row and lane:
   what was read beyond what was expected (excess), and what was expected
   beyond what was read (omission), as `gain_field` already splits a word
   forecast. Both are kept, graded, summed over rows: two numbers for a
   look.
3. *At the glance every word bracket gets its surprise* the same way,
   one `expect` for each word with that word left out. A later look
   replaces the surprise of the brackets it covers; a bracket of several
   words has the sum of theirs (*default*; amended by §68.81: a look
   replaces a word's surprise only when its bracket is that one word).
4. *`attend` reads each bracket's surprise* through the zero-started map
   of §60.1, rule 9 (*default*), so that before any teaching `attend`
   scores as it does on the starting source.
5. *The prior goes:* `BracketKeys._codebook_retrieval_prior`, its call in
   `stage_input`, and `local_prior` in `narrow_step`. Priming still
   reaches `attend` through rule 9 of §60.1.
6. *Unchanged:* `open_prediction` at the open pass, whose field the
   readers of `_expected_knowing` read (priming, `rule_order`,
   `InterpretLayer.preferred_objects`); the teacher of `expect`; the
   percept and word forecasts at an interpreted word. A look's comparison
   is reported and is not a further cost (*default*).

*On "This is Felix."* The glance reads four brackets and takes four
forecasts: `Felix` is forecast from `This`, `is` and `.`, and so on. A
word the context predicts reads with little surprise, a new name with
much. `attend` sees four pairs of numbers before its first act, where it
sees one prior today. A later look into `Felix`'s parts forecasts them
from everything outside them, the other words and `Felix`'s other
parts.

*Cost* (not measured). One `expect` for each word at the glance and one
for each later look. On the lesson's configuration the block of order
zero has some 2,300 rows. At the production size (about 600,000 rows,
hidden width 64) one call is about 77 million multiply-adds, and a
sentence of twenty looks about 1.5 billion.

### 62.4 Certificates, in outline

1. A look's forecast reads nothing inside its bracket: changing what is
   inside changes the look's field and not its forecast.
2. With the forecast equal to the look's field, the surprise is zero on
   both lanes; an unexpected word gives excess, an expected word that is
   missing gives omission.
3. At the glance every word bracket has a surprise, and a later look
   replaces the surprise of exactly the brackets it covers.
4. With the map of §60.1, rule 9, at zero, `attend` scores as on the
   starting source less the prior; the prior is in no source file.
5. Both stopping gates pass.

### 62.5 For Alec: where a look's forecast comes from

*Recommended: from everything seen except the look's place* (§62.3). It
forecasts "there", as you put it, uses the teacher `expect` already has,
and works for a look at any place and in any order.

*The other choice: from what has been understood so far.* `expect` is
taken on the field of the words the grammar has interpreted and nothing
else, and forecasts what comes next, with no place. This was Claude's
default 2 of §54.4. It is causal (it never sees the glance), and read in
order it forecasts the next word; read out of order, its forecast is not
about the place looked at.

*Answered (Alec, 2026-11-16):* "Yes, span left out". §62.3 stands as
written, and Claude's default 2 of §54.4 (a forecast takes no place) is
withdrawn.

### 63.1 Checked

  `bin/` changed: `WholeSpace.property_rows_for_bytes` intersects the
  bytes' signatures; `SparseLayer._fold_weights` nets each pair on its
  own row and is the one place every `fold_presence` call reads.
- The return stops for a question and claims no final measurement. The
  lesson and sweep it interrupted ran a variant that is now removed.
- *Recorded:* an old checkpoint keeps its words' old wholes (for
  example `This` keeps the capital property); no migration is made. A
  model trained before this repair should be trained again rather than
  loaded, if its words' readings matter.

### 63.2 The derivative at a zero sum (§58.5)

Codex is right, in Claude's reading. With one signed weight s = w - v,
the source enters with the positive part of s and the opposite with the
negative part, and at s = 0 both floors pass their derivatives: the
derivative with respect to s is g - h. That is the derivative of the one
signed weight Alec decided (§57.9) and that item 1.7 builds; it is zero
exactly where the two poles' local derivatives are equal, and nowhere
else. Choosing one pole to keep a nonzero derivative is a preference
with no reason, which Codex removed; and the removed preference stopped
a word in the grounded fixture from learning its negation.

*Recommended amendment of certificate 5 of §57.6:* "The two weights of a
pair receive gradients of equal size and opposite sign: with g and h the
derivatives that each pole's weight would receive at zero, the source
receives g - h and the opposite h - g, at equal weights as elsewhere."
