**What the forecast's numbers say, and do not.** In the lesson `expect`
was never taught: Codex reports no active omission target on any of the
160 presentations. Its forecast is therefore zero, the omission is zero
on all 5,049 comparisons, and the excess is simply how much was read at
the place. The distribution of §64.5 is a count of active rows and says
nothing yet about a forecast. This is a learning result (§43) and is
recorded, not repaired.

**Finding 1: after training, almost no word is offered to the grammar.**

*In plain terms.* Each word is read on two lanes: evidence *for* a
concept and evidence *against* it. A word may be interpreted only when
its reading has one lane (Alec, 2026-11-15: a known word "CANNOT be
minted if both lanes are active at once"). The source decides "has this
lane" by asking whether the value is above zero
(`Attention.narrowing_view`: `pooled_poles[...,1]>0`). After the lesson,
"Felix" reads for 1.0 and against 0.0002. That is above zero, so the
word counts as read with both lanes, is never offered, and
`interpretBias` is never consulted for it.

*Measured, from Codex's records of this run.*

- The 45 probes after training: 8 of 184 word places are interpreted,
  115 are looked at and found with both lanes, 61 are never looked at
  alone; 37 of 45 kept trees are empty (§64.4).
- In training the share grows. Of the words read in each fifth of the
  160 presentations, those with any evidence against: 1 of 96, 0 of 96,
  4 of 117, 30 of 118, and 117 of 117.
- Reading stops with it. In the first 64 presentations 414 word
  comparisons end interpreted and 2 left; in the last 32, 6 and 284.
- The looks grow with it. A sentence's looks after the first, summed
  over each 16 presentations: 177, 126, 112, 171, 258, 294, 189, 590,
  884, 1,021. In the last 32 presentations every one of them holds a
  reading with both lanes, and each sentence spends its whole allowance
  of 64.
- The size of the evidence against, over the 285 word readings that
  have any: smallest 0.00000006, median 0.00005, largest 0.00024. The
  evidence for is 1.0, or 0.99996.
- Every one of them has it from one source: property 0 of WholeSpace.

*The producer.* A whole property's evidence for a byte is its learned
membership, a number from 0 to 1
(`PerceptProperties.coefficients`), and its evidence against is one
minus that (`on_counts` with `complement`). The memberships are
parameters and are taught. Once teaching has moved one from 1 to 0.9998,
the evidence against is 0.0002. So the two lanes of such a reading sum
to one, and the test reads "0.9998 for" as "for and against".

*It is new.* The test is unchanged, and before the loop every one of
the 184 places was accepted after the same lesson (§59.74: "All 184
assessed word places are minted"). So either nothing moved the
memberships of property 0 then, or the walk did not read them where it
reads them now. *Not traced by me:* which cost moves them, and since
which commit.

*What item 1.8 rests on.* §57.8: "a percept that is exactly present
reads exactly 1", and "A reading in proportion to the weight comes with
item 1.7's arithmetic"; so "The question of §57.7 about the walk's test
for a mint does not arise." That question was what "both lanes active
at once" means for graded lanes, which §57.7 left to Alec. A membership
at 0.9998 is a graded value arriving one item early.

*Simulated (mine; a scratch copy and a wrapper, no source changed).*
The same lesson from the same starting random streams, with one change
in a wrapper: where the walk reads a word's lanes
(`native_word_poles`), an against lane under one hundredth of the for
lane is not counted. The cut is a device of the simulation and no
proposal.

- Through 150 of the 160 presentations every word offered is
  interpreted: 1,120 word comparisons end interpreted and none left,
  where the run as built has 857 and 370 over all 160.
- The memberships drift there as well (70 word readings with evidence
  against, the largest 0.00035), so the drift does not depend on which
  words are offered.
- At presentation 150 the run stopped at a kept close.
  `MemoryLink.link` raised "a link requires containment with its
  collection": it asks that one of the two shares `match` returns equal
  1 exactly. So the simulation gives no assessment after training.
  *Not established:* whether that stop is an artifact of the wrapper,
  which changes the walk's reading and not the values deposited, or a
  second exact test met by a graded value.

**Finding 2: a look at several words reads nothing.**

*Measured.* On a fresh model, three sentences: each of the 14 looks at
a bracket of two or more words has an empty field, and each look at one
word reads that word's concepts (1 or 8 values). In Codex's lesson all
1,606 comparisons at a look of several words are exactly (0, 0).

*Why (read, not traced to the row).* `SentenceLooks.perceive` reads the
look's extent as one bracket (`cs_read_memberships`), as rule 3 of §60.1
says in my words. A concept's features are read as a conjunction over
that bracket, and a whole property must hold on every byte of it. The
first look is different: it reads every word bracket in parallel
(rule 2). I accepted `perceive` in §68.78 without reading the field of a
look at several words; the miss is mine.

*What follows.*

- "Every look is perceived and conceptualized" holds today only at a
  bracket that is exactly one word. What a look at another place
  conceives is rule 32 of item 1.7 (a look returns percept indices, and
  a Pi finds what is there; sigma-pi §19.28 and §19.30). It is not
  repaired in item 1.8.
- The forecast's rule 3 (§62.3: "a later look replaces the surprise of
  the brackets it covers") then writes (0, 0) over every word the look
  covers. On "Felix is a cat." the glance gives the words 8, 8, 1 and 8;
  the first division looks at "is a cat." and sets its words to 0. The
  signal to `attend` is erased where attention has not yet looked.
  *Amended (my default, mine to amend):* a look replaces the pair of a
  word only when the look's bracket is that one word; a look at

## 69. The thought replay (§68.31; Codex, 2026-11-18)

### 69.1 Producer, repair and regression

The executor merges an inference with the chunks **currently held** at
the same role references and role mask. `ThoughtChunks._write_serial`
records exactly those pairs in `_alternative_pairs`; `ThoughtChunks.stage`
copies them into the inference event's `alternatives`. Replay already
read those alternatives, but also took the maximum of every earlier
inference under the same reference tuple for the entire episode. An
intervening `exist` can replace the focus; the episode maximum then
resurrected evidence no longer present in the executor.

`bin/Thoughts.py::replay_thoughts` removes only that `conclusions`
accumulator, in both derivation branches and at episode begin. Explicit
derivation still uses `ThoughtInference.replay_pair`, including its
recorded alternatives. Intuition derivation still joins its own
firings with its recorded alternatives. Every support comparison and
exception remains. The separate pervasion accumulator `implicit` is
unchanged. This builds Claude's default that the executor is the
behavior and replay checks it; no evidence against that choice was
found.

`test_thought_intuition.py::test_replay_uses_the_inferences_resident_alternatives_after_exist`
is parameterized over `derivation` and `intuition_derivation`. It gives
both inferences valid individual histories, then the three events:
infer with alternatives `(1,1)`, exist leaving `(0,0)`, infer with
alternatives `(0,0)`, all with references `(None,None,None)`. Both
parameters fail on the starting source and pass with the repair. The
same test changes the last thought's support, then the finish's support;
both corruptions still raise. The two whole thought files and both
stopping gates give **59 passed in 10.96 s**.

The proof writers are `ThoughtInference.derive` for an explicit held
premise and rule, its selected-intuition branch, and `Intuition.implication`
for a one-operand search. `ThoughtStream.materialize` labels the
producing operation. The shared serial stage records alternatives for
either proof branch after `_write_serial` has combined them. A backward
open subgoal does not combine closed evidence. No writer needs an edit.
The native census additionally checks that every combined pair reaches
the event, without adding a production validation or changing a read.

### 69.2 Anonymous-reference audit (behavior unchanged)

| Reader | What all-None equality can identify; consequence if it matched nothing |
| --- | --- |
| `ThoughtChunks._write_serial` | A held chunk with the same role mask, excluding intuition-only deposits. It does not compare numerical roles. Excluding anonymous keys would stop their pair union and the updates to other matching slots. |
| `Thoughts.replay_thoughts` | The removed `conclusions` maximum used this tuple alone. The surviving `implicit` pervasion accumulator and final judgement also use it, but native `Intuition.pervasion` requires referenced subject and property, so it cannot produce an all-None key. Rejecting such a fabricated key would reject a fabricated anonymous pervasion finish, not change a native pervasion. |
| `ThoughtStream.candidates` | The resident value at the result's exact chunk time replaces the recorded value when references agree. Excluding all-None would remove those anonymous result operands from the menu, even at their valid resident address. |
| `ThoughtStream.completion_result.same` | Attaches a proof to the finish only after references, polarity, witnesses, open slots, mask, numerical roles and recursive constituents agree. Excluding all-None would discard proofs of otherwise identical anonymous content. |
| `ThoughtStream.integrate` | When operation signatures agree, matching request/goal references allow filling the goal. Excluding all-None would continue to later integration branches instead; earlier query/result branches are unaffected. |
| `ThoughtStream.write` | Reuses an unchanged witnessed chain at its exact retained address after references, mask and numerical roles agree. Excluding all-None would lose that reuse and proceed to the writer. |
| `ThoughtStream.commit` | Reuses the exact query occurrence only after references, polarity, scope, sentence kind, pair, slots, mask and roles agree. Excluding all-None would lose this unchanged-content reuse; the separate unresolved-question reuse still exists. |
| `ThoughtInference.derive` | A constituent antecedent whose references equal the premise's is an identity match. Excluding all-None would try the subsequent membership branch, which can itself accept matching absent individual ends; rejecting the tuple alone would not necessarily reject that inference. |
| `Models._commit_sentence` | Reuses the input writer's canonical meaning after a thought leaves references, polarity, scope, evidence, slots, mask and roles unchanged. Excluding all-None would retain the thought's value instead of taking this canonical reuse. |

Two additional uses identify **requests**, not conclusions or held
chunks: `ThoughtStream.candidates` deduplicates `(role_refs, bindings)`,
and `GrammaticalThoughtRegistry.controller_candidates` deduplicates
an operation's complete result request by references, bindings and
numerical roles. Removing anonymous equality there could add duplicate
menu requests. No reference-key policy is changed in this repair.

local receipts, not production additions.

## 70. One match of a content against conceptual space (Claude, 2026-11-18; a design for Alec; no text for Codex)

Alec, 2026-11-18 (§68.67): "So it seems we should match the object, not
the word. We also have to match the object against types: it may be a
type matching a token or vice versa. And we have to account for
polysemy. To take the time to make an algorithm that matches a content
against Conceptual Space, so that we do this only in one place for all
clients needing a match." And: "WRT place/time match, they are necessary
at the level of events ... it is really generalization that should
remove that information, not us by hand outside of the matching
function I mentioned."

This section says what the source has today and proposes the form of
that one function. The requirements are his (§68.67, points 1 to 5).
The form is Claude's and nothing of it is decided. It ends with three
questions.

### 70.1 What the source has today

A search of `bin/*.py` on 2026-11-18, on Codex's working tree of
§59.75, found about forty places that compare a content with stored
candidates or choose among them. It was made by a sub-agent. Claude
read the entries marked * itself; the rest is the agent's reading.

| Family | Where | Compared | Measure | Order | Place and time |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A. A mention against held identities | `STMChunks.bind_menu`*; `ReferenceClose.score_order`*; `MemoryLink.menu` and `link`; `MediumTermMemory.merge`; `ReferenceClose.individuals` | the slot's value against off-stack chunks; a reference's content against MTM's tokens and individuals | the two numbers of `IdentityRows.meet_ratios`*, one of them exactly 1; in the scorer, then a linear policy over twelve features | must be equal, or open | cut out by `IdentityRows.coordinates`* in the scorer, the link and `individuals`; left in for a percept collection and in `merge`; in the menu, whatever lies after `meaning_start` |
| B. A content against rows of concepts | `FieldProjection.stimulate`* (every allocated row); `ConceptTrust.observe`; `ConceptHierarchy.fit`; `PartsOfSpeech.value_scores`; `BindingAnswers.cost`; `CompoundLayer.select_view`; `TimelineRead.case_coverage`; `BasicPercepts.read_points` | a point against codes, extensions or bounds | one of the two numbers, graded | `stimulate` keeps the rows of the order asked for, then folds the definitions upward | `stimulate` reads the percept block whole, place and time in it, for a row with no meaning |
| C. Likeness | `MediumTermMemory.match_candidate`; `FamiliarTier.witnessed_match` and `observe_field`; `readback_scores` and three other reads of a word from a vector | whole vectors, or the form block | a cosine against a threshold, or the greatest | equal, in MTM | left in |
| D. Distance | `Expectation.match_symbols`; `LanguageSpace.decoder_eligibility` | whole vectors; the form block | a squared distance within a tolerance | a mask | left in |
| E. A key, not a content | `InterpretLayer.word_for_form`, `lookup_word`, `preferred_objects`*; `ReferenceContext.resolve_order`; `STMChunks.refresh` | an id, a key or a form | equality; `preferred_objects` compares nothing and takes the object the context expects, then the higher order | read from the key | none |
| F. Recall | `EpisodicMemory.matches` | sets of concept ids | a product over equal ids, for each order | for each order | none |

Seven facts follow from it.

1. *One function already matches a content against all of conceptual
   space:* `FieldProjection.stimulate` ("Candidate coverage on each
   lane, then upward definition closure"). For every allocated row it
   takes how much of the row is found in the content, for and against;
   a row with meaning is read on its meaning lanes and a row without on
   its percept block; then the definitions are folded upward, so that a
   token implies its type. It is called in three places.
2. *Every other reader compares a content with a short list it holds,*
   and chooses its own coordinates and its own measure.
3. *The two numbers are already there.* Every reader of family A takes
   both numbers of `meet_ratios`: how much of the candidate is found in
   the content, and how much of the content is found in the candidate.
4. *Place and time are removed by hand in five places:*
   `IdentityRows.carrier`* ("excluding its separate location/time
   band"), `IdentityRows.coordinates`*, `GrammarLayer.content_operand`,
   `MereologicalCodes.remember_content`*, and §59.71's
   `STMChunks.bind_menu`*. Elsewhere they are left in the vector that is
   compared.
5. *Nothing but `stimulate`'s fold relates two orders.* Family A
   refuses a candidate of another order.
6. *A word with several objects is never matched by content.*
   `preferred_objects` takes one before anything is compared.
7. *A miss makes something new in six places,* each in its own way:
   `ReferenceClose`'s preview and commit (`open_reference`);
   `MemoryLink.link` (`pool.open`, `append_path`);
   `FamiliarTier.observe_candidate` (`open_candidate`, then
   `promote_candidates`); `InterpretLayer.lookup_word` and `reading`
   (`pool.named`); `PerceptCollections.observe`*;
   `EntryRead.recall_identities`.

### 70.2 The proposal

1. *One function, in one module* (*default names:* `ConceptualMatch`,
   `match`). It takes a content and the rows to match it against; with
   no rows given, every allocated row, as `stimulate` does. For each
   row and each lane it gives the two numbers of fact 3. It chooses
   nothing. `stimulate` becomes its call over every row.
2. *The measure is the one that is there.* "The row is found in the
   content": a token implies its type, and a whole implies its part.
   "The content is found in the row": a description fits a token.
   *Claude's reading:* at one order these are Alec's "a type matching a
   token or vice versa". A client that needs exactness asks for a ratio
   of one, as now (Alec, 2026-11-05). A client that weighs keeps the
   numbers.
3. *Content and position.* The function is the one place that knows
   which coordinates are content and which are a place or a time. It
   takes the two numbers on the content: the meaning lanes of a row
   that has meaning, the percept block of an event. Where the content
   and the row are both events it also gives the relation of their
   places and of their times, read by the codecs
   (`WhereEncoding.decode`, `RowTime`'s ages and brackets). A row that
   is a generalization holds no place and no time, so nothing is
   compared for it. That is how generalization removes them. Of fact
   4's five places, `carrier`, `coordinates` and the menu stop cutting.
   `content_operand` is the operators' and `remember_content` makes a
   key; neither is a match, and both are left (*default*).
4. *Across orders, by membership and never by codes.* At one order the
   two numbers are taken. Between orders nothing compares one order's
   code with another's (Alec, 2026-11-15: no space has geometric
   influence on another). A token reaches its type, and a type its
   tokens, through the definitions: upward as `stimulate`'s fold has it
   today, downward with item 1.7's spread (sigma-pi rule 23). The
   function gives every row it reached with its order and does not
   refuse a row for its order; a client says which relation it accepts.
5. *The object, and each object.* A client that matches a mention gives
   the content of the mention's object. A word with several objects is
   matched once for each object the context expects
   (`InterpretLayer.denotations`, in `preferred_objects`' order), and
   the result keeps them apart, so that what matches can decide among
   them. A word whose only object is blank gives no content, and
   nothing is offered for it by content (`meet_ratios`: "An empty
   request supplies no content evidence"). *Claude's reading* of "we
   don't want to match pronouns always": a pronoun is matched when it
   has an object with content, and otherwise by what it shares with a
   name in another modality (sigma-pi rule 31).
6. *A miss* (Alec's direction, §68.67, point 7). Where nothing reaches
   the client's bar the function says so, and the content goes to MTM
   as a candidate by one writer. Its recurrence makes a generalization
   (sigma-pi rules 20 and 31). *Default:* not in the first text; fact
   7's six places stay until then.
7. *Its inside in item 1.7.* The cycle's forward is the first number
   for every concept at once; the spread and `parts` and `wholes` give
   the second and the way down. The function's callers do not change
   when its inside does.

### 70.3 The clients, in the order they would move

| When | Clients | What changes for them |
|---|---|---|
| The first text | Family A (`bind_menu`, `score_order`, `MemoryLink.menu` and `link`, `merge`, `individuals`), and `stimulate` with its three calls | they call the one function; the menu gives it the mention's object; §59.71's two changes go; no reader of the family cuts coordinates |
| Later, listed and not moved | `ConceptTrust.observe`, `ConceptHierarchy.fit`, `PartsOfSpeech.value_scores`, `BindingAnswers.cost`, the case reads | graded reads of the same numbers |
| Not clients (*Claude's reading*) | the reads of a word from a vector (`readback_scores` and three others), which match forms for the reconstruction; the keys of family E; likeness in MTM, which item 1.7's rule 16 removes; recall, whose form is decided (an entry holds every order and a question is matched order by order, §3.12) | none |

### 70.4 What was checked, and what was not

- *HEAD is the trial of "match the object".* At HEAD the object reached
  the menu (§68.65, point 5): 129 candidates offered on four files
  where the word gets 18, and
  `test_public_reading_fuses_the_reference_before_capture_and_write`
  passes with place and time compared, equal in its 15 comparisons.
  Codex's own census of the four files (§59.78) gives 84 offered at
  HEAD and 58 on its source, with one real bind chosen on each. The
  runs are not seeded and its count of a candidate differs from
  §68.65's; both show the order filter refusing most of what passes
  on content (47 of 131 at HEAD, 201 of 259 now).
- *Coverage with place and time left in* (the codecs of §59.62,
  `meet_ratios`, content (.2, .2) and (.8, .8); scratch, not a
  receipt):

  | Content | Row | The row found in the content | The content found in the row |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | a description with no place | a token at place 20, tick 1 | .05 | 1.0 |
  | an occurrence at place 20, tick 1 | a type's row with no place | 1.0 | .05 |
  | an occurrence at place 20, tick 1 | the same content at place 10, tick 0 | .986 | .973 |
  | the same | the same at place 20, tick 1 | 1.0 | 1.0 |
  | a word at place 20, tick 1 | a held idea with no place | .25 | .059 |

  So an object with no place fits a token that has one, and a type is
  found in its token, with nothing removed. The last row is §59.70's

- *Coverage of the place coordinates is not a test of the same place.*
  Of 19,791 pairs of different places, in 6,291 one band lay inside the
  other; of 19,668 pairs of different times, in none. This is why point
  3 has the codecs compare positions.
- *Not tried:* the menu given the object that the read stages
  (`_ar_word_object_ids`, `_ar_word_object_rows`,
  `_ar_word_object_atoms`) while the slot keeps the word; a word with
  two objects; the cost of the function at the menu's rate. A trial on
  a scratch copy comes before any text.

### 70.8 Alec's answers (2026-11-18)

To the question whether the one match is built as §70 proposes, now, in
part B:

> Yes, as proposed

To the three questions put with it (the measure; a word with several
objects; the blank object, which is sigma-pi §19.21's open point 6):

> 1. I am not clear what you mean by measure here. an example please.
> 2. A word with several objects is polysemy, we should pick one (but
> make it an educated guess from field context/activation).
> 3. better never to have the blank at all, but to avoid a discontinuous
> decision, we might train both and remove the blank only if the vectors

And, while the trial of §70.10 ran:

> By the way, Im Ok with only spot testing this change, since codex will
> have completed a full sweep and we acknowledge that further work is
> necessary with multimodal before we can earn identity correctly.

His other remarks of the same message, on how the tie of a word and an
object is learned, are in sigma-pi §19.27.

**What it settles.**

1. The one match is built now, in part B, as §70.2 proposes, with the
   amendments below.
2. *One object for a word.* §70.2's point 5 is changed: a word with
   several objects has one picked, by an educated guess from the field's
   context and activation. Nothing is matched for each object.
   *Claude's reading:* `InterpretLayer.preferred_objects` is that guess
   as it stands (what the expected field holds, then the higher order),
   and the object the read stages for a word is its choice.
3. *Spot tests.* This change is certified by spot tests. No sweep and
   no lesson is asked for it.
4. *The measure* is not yet answered: he asked for an example, which is
   §70.9.
5. *The blank object* is item 1.7's and is recorded in sigma-pi §19.27.

**A default this adds** (*Claude's*; found by the trial of §70.10). At
the menu four mentions in five are phrases and not single words. A
phrase has no object during the read: its meaning is made at
comprehension. `doc/Architecture.md` has the bond at the read made "as
the word arrives" and the resolution at the clause end, which can undo
it. So in the first text a single word is compared by its object, and a
phrase is compared as it is today, and counted. The object of a phrase
at the menu is left for a later text. (*Reworded by §70.13, after
Alec's word on the phrase.*)

### 70.9 The measure, by an example

Take four coordinates of meaning: furry, meows, barks, black.

| | furry | meows | barks | black | total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| the description "cat" (the mention's object) | .8 | .8 | 0 | 0 | 1.6 |
| Felix, a held identity | .8 | .8 | 0 | .8 | 2.4 |
| Rex, a held identity | .8 | 0 | .8 | 0 | 1.6 |

The overlap of two rows is the sum, over the coordinates, of the
smaller of their two values. The measure is two numbers:

- *how much of the candidate is found in the content:* the overlap
  divided by the candidate's total;
- *how much of the content is found in the candidate:* the overlap
  divided by the content's total.

| Content | Candidate | Overlap | The candidate found in the content | The content found in the candidate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| "cat" | Felix | 1.6 | 1.6 / 2.4 = .67 | 1.6 / 1.6 = 1.0 |
| "cat" | Rex | .8 | .8 / 1.6 = .5 | .8 / 1.6 = .5 |
| Felix | the kind cat | 1.6 | 1.6 / 1.6 = 1.0 | 1.6 / 2.4 = .67 |

Everything the description says is true of Felix, so the second number
is 1 and Felix may be offered. Neither number is 1 for Rex, and Rex is
not offered. In the last row a token is met and its type is the
candidate: the first number is 1, which is "a token implies its type".
The rule of 2026-11-05 offers a candidate when either number is exactly
1. These are the two numbers of `IdentityRows.meet_ratios`, which every
reader of family A takes today.

*The question that stands:* whether the one function gives these two
numbers (*recommended*), or another measure, such as a likeness of the
two vectors or the layers' own activation.

### 70.12 The measure, documented; provisional (Alec, 2026-11-18)

Alec, 2026-11-18, of §70.9: "I have not reviewed the measure above, but
as long as it aims to fulfill my description, please doc it and we will
return to it."

So the measure stands for the first text as a provisional choice. It is
kept inside the one function, so that changing it is a change in one
place.

**The measure.** For a content $q$ and a candidate $c$, with
coordinates between 0 and 1, on the coordinates the function compares:

- the overlap, $m = \sum_i \min(q_i, c_i)$;
- *the candidate found in the content*, $m / \sum_i c_i$;
- *the content found in the candidate*, $m / \sum_i q_i$.

A side with no mass gives 0 ("An empty request supplies no content
evidence"). No distance and no likeness of direction enters. It is
`IdentityRows.meet_ratios`, unchanged. The example is §70.9.

**Which coordinates** (the first text). Where the codebook has no form
block, the whole code. Where it has one, the coordinates after it,
which hold the meaning lanes. For `FieldProjection.stimulate`'s rows
that have no meaning, the form block.

**What a client does with the two numbers** (unchanged). Family A
offers a candidate when either is exactly 1 (Alec, 2026-11-05), and
the scorer at the close weighs both among its twelve features.
`stimulate` writes the first as the row's evidence, for each lane.

**Against his description** (§68.67).

| His words | How the measure and the first text aim at it | Not yet met |
|---|---|---|
| "match the object, not the word" | the function's content is an object's content; where the mention is a single word the menu gives it that word's object | a phrase is still compared by its word-tree value; its object exists only at comprehension |
| "a type matching a token or vice versa" | at one order the two numbers are the two directions: a description fits a token (the second is 1), and a token implies its type (the first is 1) | between orders the menu still refuses another order; a type reaches its tokens only through `lower` and the fold upward; the way down is item 1.7's spread |
| "account for polysemy" | one object is picked for a word by the field, which is the read's choice (§70.8) | the pick is made at the read; comprehension may pick another at the end |
| "only in one place for all clients" | one function; family A and `stimulate` call it | the graded readers of §70.3's second row are listed and not moved |
| place and time "are necessary at the level of events" | where a whole vector is compared for a percept or a percept collection, its place and time are in it, as today | their coordinates are compared by coverage, which is no test of the same place (§70.4); the comparison by the codecs is not in the first text |
| "generalization ... should remove that information, not us by hand outside of the matching function" | the function alone decides the coordinates; the cut that §59.71 put in the menu goes; a concept is read on its meaning, where no place or time lies | `IdentityRows.carrier` and `coordinates` still cut for their other callers; `content_operand` and `remember_content` are left |

### 70.13 Alec on the phrase as the mention (2026-11-18)

Alec, 2026-11-18, of §70.8's default for a phrase:

> Ps: the phrase as the mention can still be turned into a concept
> vector and either created or just used as an identity in a small
> pi-not-sigma until it dictates that a symbol should be produced for
> that entity.

**What it says** (*Claude's reading*). A phrase is not left without an
object. Its concept vector is made, and that vector is the entity:
either a concept is made for it, or it is used as an identity in a
small Pi, Not, Sigma until that store dictates that a symbol be
produced for it. The small Pi, Not, Sigma is the store that tries
candidates, MTM in the form he gave it on 2026-11-17 (sigma-pi §19.21).

**What exists** (read on 2026-11-18; not run).

- *A phrase's concept vector.* At the read it is the node's value on
  the stack, composed by the operators from its words' values. At
  comprehension it is the same node composed from its words' objects
  (`Comprehension.Evaluation`: "Evaluate a completed grammatical formula
  on its referenced objects"), which walks the recorded program after
  the read, once for each scored path.
- *Used as an identity.* At the menu, the dummy alternative keeps the
  mention's own content. At the close, a description with no referent
  opens an identity in MTM with its value (`open_reference` in
  `ReferenceClose.commit`, through `MemoryLink.link`), read from
  comprehension's operands (`ClauseJournal.ComprehensionClose`).
- *Until a symbol is produced.* `FamiliarTier.promote_identity` ("A kept
  definition or recurrent mention supplies an object's witness"); in
  item 1.7, rule 20.

**The gap.** One thing. During the read, the vector the menu tests for
a phrase is the one made from its words. The one made from its objects
exists only at comprehension. To have it at the menu, comprehension
would value a part of the tree during the read; its evaluator walks a
recorded program for one stream, outside the walk of the read. That was
not tried.

**What it changes.**

- §70.8's default is reworded. A phrase at the menu is compared by its
  concept vector, and where nothing is offered or chosen it is used as
  an identity in MTM until a symbol is produced, as the close has it
  today. In the first text that vector is the one the read has: nothing
  is changed for a phrase, and it is counted.
- Step 6 of §70.11 has Codex report what it would take for
  comprehension to value a phrase during the read.
- The first row of §70.12's table stands in its third column: it is
  what remains to be met.

*Open, for Alec; it does not block the first text.* Whether the vector
of a phrase at the menu must be the one made from its objects
(*Claude's leaning:* yes, as the next text, once Codex has said what it
takes), or whether the read's own vector serves for the bond, since the
close settles the reference from comprehension's value and can undo the
bond.

### 70.14 The measure matched with parthood as *The Whole Part* defines it (Alec, 2026-11-18)

Alec, 2026-11-18: "I would like you to match the overlap measure you
have for identity with that for parthood as defined on pages 184-185 of
The Whole Part, by Alec Rogers." In the epub it is the section Logic of
the Formal Summary. And: "that definition of parthood is a 0-1 range of
the overlap between two vectors, if I have done that calculation
right."

**The book's definition** (pages 184 and 185 of *The Whole Part*, one
of the books attached to the author's ORCID record; read in the copy at
archive.org, since the download link of thewholepart.com was broken on
that day; nothing of it is quoted). Parthood is a continuous function
of two things with a value between zero and one: the size of what they
share, over the size of the first.

$$x < y \;=\; \frac{|x \cap y|}{|x|}$$

Its Figure Aa shows five relations of two shapes A and B, and its Table
Ab gives each as two values, A in B and B in A.

**The match.** Take what two vectors share as the smaller value on each
coordinate, and a size as the sum of the coordinates. Then the book's
parthood is the measure of §70.12, exactly:

- *the content found in the candidate*, $m / \sum_i q_i$, is $q < c$;
- *the candidate found in the content*, $m / \sum_i c_i$, is $c < q$.

The two numbers of the one match are the two columns of the book's
table. `IdentityRows.meet_ratios`, given regions as vectors of ones and
zeros, returns the table's values (scratch, 2026-11-18):

| The book's case | A in B | B in A | In the one match |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. apart | 0 | 0 | nothing is offered |
| 2. B inside A | .3 | 1 | the candidate is a part of the content: a token implies its type |
| 3. A inside B | 1 | .3 | the content is a part of the candidate: a description fits a token |
| 4. the same | 1 | 1 | identity |
| 5. they overlap | .2 | .2 | each is a part of the other to a degree; not offered today |

**What it shows about "identity".** The rule of 2026-11-05 offers a
candidate when either number is exactly 1. That is cases 2, 3 and 4:
parthood one way or the other. Identity is case 4 alone, parthood both
ways; `doc/Mereology.md` has `equal` as the product of the two
parthoods. So the measure that §70 has called a measure of identity is
the book's parthood, taken both ways.

**Alec's calculation.** It is right where the coordinates are zero or
more. What two such vectors share is at least 0 and at most the size of
the first, so the value lies between 0 and 1. It is 1 when the first is
at or below the second on every coordinate, and 0 when they share
nothing. Checked on 100,000 random pairs. It does not hold for signed
coordinates: on signed random vectors the same formula left the range
in 99.7 of 100 pairs. In the model a concept is stored as two unsigned
lanes, and place and time are unsigned since §59.62, so it holds
wherever the one match reads.

**Where the source differs from the book.**

1. *An empty first thing.* The formula has no value there.
   `meet_ratios` gives 0 ("An empty request supplies no content
   evidence", with the rule of 2026-11-05). `Ops._part_kernel` gives 1,
   the empty being a part of everything (`doc/Mereology.md`). The one
   match keeps 0.
2. *The parthood of `doc/Mereology.md` is another function:* "Parthood
   as Clipped Cosine Projection", the product of the two vectors over
   their lengths. It is the same both ways, so it cannot give the
   book's cases 2 and 3: it reads .548 and .548 where the book has .3
   and 1. The readers of identity do not use it. *Not asked, and not
   proposed here:* whether that function should become the book's.
3. *Two lanes.* The readers of family A sum over both lanes of the
   meaning at once, so the first is a part of the second when it is at
   or below it on the for lane and on the against lane.
   `FieldProjection.stimulate` takes each lane apart.

**What changes in §70.** The names only. "The content found in the
candidate" is the parthood of the content in the candidate, and "the
candidate found in the content" is the parthood of the candidate in the
content. The measure is the book's parthood and no longer only "the one
that is there". It stays provisional in the sense of §70.12 until Alec
has returned to it. The text of §70.11 needs no change: it names the
two numbers of `meet_ratios`.

**For the documentation pass** (`doc/*.md` is not edited now).
`doc/Mereology.md`: that the measure of identity is the parthood of
*The Whole Part*, pages 184 and 185, taken both ways, with the table
above, and beside it what the clipped cosine is used for.
`doc/Architecture.md`, the paragraph on a mention's association: the
same reference.

### 70.15 Parthood in the docs, signed values, and identity in MTM (Alec, 2026-11-18)

Alec, 2026-11-18, of §70.14:

> I think we need to replace doc/Mereology.md parthood: a clipped cosine
> is symmetric (?), "which is the same both ways. It reads .548 and .548
> where your table has .3 and 1." parthood is not symmetric. So please
> update that doc reference, and lets use it to define identity where
> you are using that measure in MTM, but lets also figure out how it can
> be extended to signed values (my guess is that, per dimension, there
> is no overlap between a negative and positive value)

> Note that I am not proposing we replace all inner product with this
> formula, because that might be quite slow over global concept
> comparisons, but it seems like a good fit for MTM and perhaps other
> places.

**1. The doc.** `doc/Mereology.md` is changed. Its section "Parthood as
Clipped Cosine Projection" is now "Parthood as Shared Size": the book's
function, that it is not symmetric, the five relations by its two
directions, signed values, the empty operand, and what the source
computes today. With it: `part()` as the graded form of `Ops.partOf`;
"Identity is decided by parthood, not distance"; the suite's table; the
five-relation table, whose old conditions could not hold for a part
that is three tenths of its whole; and the claim of Boole's
contrapositive, which held only because the cosine is the same both
ways. `doc/FutureWork.md` has one sentence and its link changed.
*Left as they are, because they describe `Ops._part_kernel` as built:*
`doc/Logic.md` ("Sign and parthood", "Parthood as Projection"),
`doc/Architecture.md` (two sentences) and `doc/STM.md` (one link text).
They change with point 5.

**2. Signed values: his guess is right, and the stored form already
computes it.** On each coordinate two values of the same sign share the
smaller of their sizes, two of opposite signs share nothing, and a size
is the sum of the absolute values. That is the unsigned parthood on a
signed value's two lanes, for and against. Checked on 100,000 random
signed pairs against `ConceptualMatch.match` on the two lanes: the
difference is 0.0 in both directions. Also checked:

- the value lies between 0 and 1;
- a thing is wholly a part of itself, and no part of its negation;
- negating both changes nothing;
- it is 1 exactly when every coordinate of the first lies between zero
  and the same coordinate of the second; a coordinate on the other side
  takes away exactly its own share;
- `Ops.partOf`'s test, each coordinate at or below the other's, is not
  this on signed values: (-.9, .1) is at or below (.2, .5) on both
  coordinates, and its parthood in it is .1;
- the contrapositive does not hold for the exchange of lanes: it gives
  the other direction.

**3. Identity in MTM.** The readers of this measure in MTM are
`MediumTermMemory.merge`, `MemoryLink.menu` and `link`, and
`ReferenceClose.individuals`. Since `31b24db620` each calls
`ConceptualMatch.match` on the stored lanes, so each computes the
book's parthood, signed values included. The doc now defines the terms:
one is a part of the other when one of the two numbers is 1, and two
are the same when both are. Those readers admit on parthood one way,
as before; nothing in the source changes by this point.

**4. Not every inner product** (Alec). A likeness stays where every
concept is compared at once. MTM's own remaining matchers are
likenesses too: `MediumTermMemory.match_candidate` and
`FamiliarTier.witnessed_match` (a cosine of .8 or more, after an exact
test of proportions) and `FamiliarTier.observe_field` (a cosine of .8,
and of .5). MTM holds 64 entries, so the cost of parthood there is
nothing. What would change is the meaning: a cosine ignores size, and
size is certainty in this space, so two centroids of one direction and
different certainty are the same by cosine and, by parthood, the weaker
is a part of the stronger. *Not tried.* Item 1.7's rule 16 (likeness of
codes pairs nothing) rebuilds these readers.

**5. The function the source calls parthood.** `Ops._part_kernel` with
`scalar=True` is the clipped cosine. It has four callers: the support
of the thought `part` (`ThoughtFaces.part`), the same in a query
(`bin/Queries.py`), a score of consistency (`_part_score` in
`bin/Layers.py`), and `ImpenetrableLayer`, which no production path
builds. Each compares two vectors, not all concepts. With the cosine
the support of "A is a part of B" is the support of "B is a part of A".
*Trial* (a scratch copy of `31b24db620` with the book's signed parthood
in that branch; the 58 test files that touch parthood, and both gates;
not a receipt):

| Source | Passed | Skipped | Failed |
|---|---|---|---|
| as committed (the 58 files) | 1,245 | 15 | 0 |
| with the book's parthood (the 58 files and both gates) | 1,241 | 15 | 6 |

Both gates pass. The six are the tests that state the cosine's own
properties: five of `test_basicmodel.py::TestBasisMereology`
(`test_part_is_clipped_cosine`,
`test_part_satisfies_boole_contrapositive`,
`test_boundary_zero_under_clipped_cosine`,
`test_overlap_false_when_parallel`,
`test_equal_three_region_partition`) and
`test_impenetrable.py::TestOverlapPenalty::test_relation_counts_partition_non_diagonal`.
One thing to settle with it: `Ops.copart`'s scalar is one less the
parthood of the first in the second, and its docstring calls it the
part of the second that the first does not account for.

**Open, for Alec.**

1. Whether `Ops._part_kernel`'s scalar form becomes the book's parthood
   (*recommended:* yes; it is "perhaps other places", it compares two
   vectors, and six definitional tests are ported).
2. Whether MTM's three likeness matchers move to parthood now, after a

## 74. How the attend logic is split over items 1.8, 1.7 and 1.5 (Claude, at Alec's request, 2026-11-18)

Alec, 2026-11-18: "Please see the sentence optimization of 1.5 and
decide how this attend logic should be split". The decision below is
Claude's, and Alec may overrule it.

**The two things to fit together.** For item 1.5's sentence
optimization, Alec on 2026-11-17: "compute perceptual features for the
whole sentence at the start (IOW, do all codebook lookups by building
an array of percept indices for the .what and an array of .where with
the same indices)". For a look, Alec on 2026-11-18: "A look should be a
.where that returns percept indices." They are one design. The sentence
is perceived once into two arrays, and a look is a mask on the second
that returns indices into the first.

**The contract of a look, the same in all three items.**

1. A sentence's percepts are two arrays made at its start: the percept
   indices, and their `.where`, with the same indices. They exist
   today: `native_indices` and `native_part_spans` of the perceptual
   space's forward input.
2. A look is a `.where`. It returns the indices whose `.where` lies in
   it. Nothing else names a look: not a word's ordinal, and not a slot
   of the slab.
3. What a look computes, its memberships, its percepts and its
   concepts, is a function of the two arrays and the mask, and of
   nothing that another look computed.
4. The arrays do not change inside a sentence, since admission and
   nomination are at its boundaries.

**Alec's note on it** (2026-11-18): "it does suggest building the
mereology, but leaving the PI to create basic percepts as something
that changes in dependence on the .where supplied by the attend()
mechanism." So the line between the two is this.

- *Once for a sentence: the mereology.* The parts and the wholes of
  the sentence at their places. They are what the two arrays hold,
  and what item 1.5 gathers once.
- *At each look: the Pi.* It makes the basic percepts from those
  parts and wholes, and what it makes changes with the `.where` that
  `attend` supplies. A basic percept is never made ahead for the
  sentence.

Where this section says "percepts" of the two arrays, it means those
parts and wholes, and not the basic percepts of item 1.7.

**The split.**

| Part | Item | What it builds | What it leaves for later |
|---|---|---|---|
| The loop | 1.8 (§60, being built) | `attend` again and again; every look perceived; `interpret` at a look; one chooser; the allowance; `unfocus`; the teacher | A look is still a bracket of whole word intervals, and its word is found by the exact lookup. Each look reads its percepts again from the arrays, with the row lookups that costs |
| What a look is | 1.7 (its rule 32) | A look is any `.where`. Behind the mask the Pi finds the spellings and returns the basic percept. Hit and miss feed the width of its cone. The stem's word intervals are no longer the unit of a look | The cost: the rows are still looked up at each look |
| What a look costs | 1.5, part 2 (the percept pass) | The rows of the parts and wholes are gathered once, beside the `.where` array, at the sentence's start. A look is one masked product on the device, the Pi on them, with no lookup and no host read after the start | nothing |

**Why this order.** What a look does comes first and what it costs
last. Item 1.5 is certified by results equal to the path before it. If
it came before item 1.7, that equality would be certified against a
read that item 1.7 then replaces.

**So that nothing is built twice.**

1. *In item 1.8.* A look's perception (rule 3 of §60.1) reads the two
   arrays at the look's extent, as the first look does
   (`FamiliarTier.open_sentence`). No structure is added for a look
   that is keyed by a word's ordinal. The text of §68.75 has the line.
2. *In item 1.7.* The look's read is written as the mask and then the
   Pi, with no reference to word intervals. One certificate for it: a
   look with the same mask gives the same result whatever was looked at
   before it.
3. *In item 1.5.* Three lines of its list were written on 2026-10-30,
   before the loop of looks, and change:
   - "the percept pass runs once per sentence over all words" is over
     the sentence's parts and wholes, since a look is no longer made
     of words; the basic percepts are made at each look.
   - "the forecast scored for all words at once" is withdrawn in that
     form. By rule 7 of §60.1 a word's forecast is made at its look and
     reads only the words found before it. What does not depend on the
     order found, the target rows of every word, is gathered once.
   - "a known word's percept read from its identity row's `amax`" is
     superseded by rule 32 of item 1.7: a word's basic percept is what
     the Pi's row returns.
   Unchanged: ragged parts in place of the 64-wide padding; and an
   explore path resumed from `SentenceFork`'s state, which rule 12 of
   §60.1 begins (a departing path reuses the looks and the bricks
   before its departure).
4. *The word's lookup is not part of the percept pass.* In item 1.8 it
   is the staged bank's exact lookup, and in item 1.7 it is the Pi's
   row.

**The number item 1.5 is held to** (the wiring document, section 7):
1,924 lookups of codebook rows for a sentence, 63 of them of a whole
table. After item 1.5: the lookups of the sentence's start, and none
after it. *Not checked:* how many of the 1,924 are made at looks, since
the measurement is older than the loop of looks.

## 75. Codex does not wait on a question: it proposes, builds and goes on (Alec, 2026-11-18)

Alec, 2026-11-18:

> also, codex is sitting idle for much of the time, it would be nice if
> we enabled it to do more work instead of blocking on questions. Can
> it propose the solution itself? its a capable mind, and we still have
> oppostunity to review.

This widens §73. Of its three places where Codex still stopped, the
first two were Claude's reading, and the second is withdrawn.

**The rule.**

1. *A question is not a stop.* Where two solutions differ in design and
   the specification does not choose, Codex writes the question, the
   solutions it sees and the one it recommends, builds the one it
   recommends, and goes on. It is marked in the return as provisional,
   and it is in a commit of its own so that it can be taken back.
   Claude reviews it with the return, and Alec may overrule it then.
2. *A recorded decision of Alec's is not overturned in the source.*
   Where Codex's recommendation would go against one, it builds the
   path that keeps the decision, writes its proposal, and goes on with
   everything that does not depend on the answer. (*Claude's reading;
   his to widen.*)
3. *The standing rules hold as before* (§73, point 3): no changed
   bound, learning rate, seed, capacity or presentation count; no
   validation weakened or removed; a learning certificate recorded and
   not repaired; no push.
4. *No idle time.* A text for Codex names what comes after it. When a
   text is finished, or what is left of it waits on an answer, Codex
   takes the next thing named, without waiting for a review between.

**What changes.** Every text for Codex from §68.84 on is written so.
The text of item 1.7 (`doc/plans/2026-11-14-sigma-pi-layers.md`,
§19.8) is rewritten before it is carried in any case (sigma-pi
§19.44), and takes this rule then.
